title: SS Rajamouli hails Nitesh Tiwari and Namit Malhotra for bringing the story of Ramayana to the screen on such a grand scale
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor , is among the most anticipated films of the year. The movie features some of the biggest names in the Hindi movie industry, with Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita.

Adding to this, SS Rajamouli has showed support for the rollout of Ramayana. Envisioned as a two-part epic, the movie will bring the story of the Ramayana to the big screen on a grand scale. The first instalment is scheduled to rollout worldwide on November 5, 2026, followed by Part 2 in Diwali 2027. The films are planned for rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

Meanwhile, The makers have rolled out the new trailer of the movie, giving audiences their spectacular new glimpse of Nitesh Tiwari’s ambitious take on one of India’s most celebrated epics. Filmmaker SS Rajamouli has now shared the trailer and showed support for the movie ahead of its rollout. Taking to X, Rajamouli wrote, “#Ramayana is a story every Indian storyteller grows up aspiring to tell. It's a joy to see @niteshtiwari22 and @malhotra_namit bring it to the screen on such a grand scale. Each star brings these timeless characters to life with depth.”
Notably, “Looking forward to 5th November. Best wishes to the entire team,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, The 2-minute 36-second trailer shows new footage and more moments featuring Ram and Ravana. The trailer opens with a voice describing a time when the world lived in harmony, saying, “Before history was written... men walked among gods... and the world existed in perfect order.” It finally shows Kunal Kapoor playing the role of Lord Indra. That peace is soon threatened by Ravana, whose rise to power changes the course of the world. The narration continues, “But from the darkness rose an evil force... Ravana. Born from fire and fury, he bent the gods to his will and made the world his throne.”

In further updates, Ranbir Kapoor's Rama is shown grappling with the responsibility that comes with his destiny. Determined to stop Ravana, he says, “If this is my fate... I will not hesitate to destroy him. If I don't stop him... the world will fall.” The trailer closes on a foreboding note, with Ravana warning, “This is just... the beginning.”

On top of that, The first trailer had drawn criticism from some viewers for its visual effects, sparking debate about the movie's CGI and overall look. The team has urged audiences to wait for the finished movie and experience it in theatres before reaching a final verdict. But the fresh new English international trailer shows the movie as a massive epic.

Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is being planned as a theatrical event, with releases in 3D, IMAX and other premium large formats. The makers have promised “the most immersive 3D cinematic experience ever," putting the movie's visual scale and big-screen presentation at the centre of its appeal.

title: SC panel launches portal for complaints, evidence on use of pellet guns, violence during July protest at Jantar Mantar
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court-appointed High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC), tasked with inquiring into violence at Jantar Mantar , Delhi, and other places outside Delhi during the CJP protests in July has opened an online portal for people to upload complaints and representations, according to a Home Ministry statement on Saturday.

Adding to this, File photo of A Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) supporters shouting slogans at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on July 23, 2026 during the protest to demand the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged NEET exam irregularities (AFP) The statement added that priority will be given to complaints of pellet use and harassment of female protesters among others. Track live updates on CJP protest

Meanwhile, “The HPEC shall examine all issues enumerated in paragraphs 12 and 13 of the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s Order dated August 18, 2026, and paragraph 5(i) of the order dated September 10, 2026. Priority will be given to matters pertaining to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protestors, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side,” a government statement shared.

Notably, The paragraphs mentioned in the two SC orders are about the same issues: use of pellets, electric batons, violence against protesters, including police personnel, compensation, and targeted violence.

As per the latest buzz, The statement shared that the portal http://hpec.nic.in has been launched for the convenience of the affected people including victims among police and other security forces during the protests.

In further updates, “The Portal is designed in such a manner as to enable due protection to vulnerable witnesses and also to keep the identities confidential and undisclosed, if so wished by the affected persons. The affected persons and other stakeholders are encouraged to access the portal and upload their complaints/representations making use of the formats as applicable, “the statement shared adding that those who wish to submit the complaints submit the complaints, can do so at the Office of the HPEC at Shiksha Sadan, 17, Rouse Avenue Institutional Area, New Delhi 110002 between 1400 hrs. and 1600 Hrs. on all working days.
On top of that, “Submissions can also be sent by post at the above address or by email at hpec2026.enquiry[at]nic[dot]in,” the statement shared.

HT checked the portal, where one can submit information in four different ways: as an affected person (including police personnel), those who want to submit complaints or are witnesses but wish to remain anonymous, the third is for submitting any other information confidentially, and the fourth is for those with suggestions for the HPEC. For each category, there are different questions along with the option to attach complaints. There is also a question to check if the victim was sexually assaulted. One can also post videos and photographs of the injuries, the incident or the medical reports.

title: Congress gets Delhi Police nod for Ramlila Maidan rally amid SIR protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
A No Objection Certificate (NOC) has been issued to the Congress for a rally at Ramlila Maidan, shared Delhi Police on Saturday.

Adding to this, The Congress's proposed rally comes amid a broader row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. (AICC) In conversation with ANI, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Central Rohit Rajbir Singh shared the ground will be booked from October 25 to November 3.

Meanwhile, This follows Jantar Mantar being de-notified as a designated venue for organising protests and demonstrations in Delhi. The Delhi Police has designated three alternative locations for holding such activities. The three new designated protest venues are Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi.

Notably, The DCP shared that the Congress first asked the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) about availability, which shared the ground would be free from October 25 to November 3. "The MCD shared that the venue would be available from October 25 to November 3. After receiving the venue availability certificate, the Congress party approached us," he shared.

As per the latest buzz, "After interacting with them and understanding the security arrangements required, we decided to grant them the No Objection Certificate (NOC). We issued it today. They will now take the certificate back to the MCD, which is the owning agency responsible for the land, and then begin their preparations. The ground will be booked from October 25 to November 3," he added.
In further updates, DCP Singh further shared that any other stakeholder or organiser wanting to book the ground may also follow the same process.

On top of that, The Congress's proposed rally comes amid a broader row over the Special Intensive Revision ( SIR ) of electoral rolls, which has escalated over the weeks as multiple protests erupted in the national capital led by INDIA Bloc and activists. The opposition camp has been demanding the roll-back of SIR and resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The protests also witnessed a police crackdown as over a hundred of demonstrators were detained amid heightened security in central Delhi. Congress has been staging continuous protests against the CEC, with INDIA Bloc allies joining the chorus.

title: Falguni Pathak’s Maine Payal Hai Chhankai girl Himani Shah sparks nostalgia with old clip, jokes she hasn’t topped that career high
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Navratri and garba festivities are incomplete without Falguni Pathak’s iconic numbers. Star and model Himani Shah, who starred in Falguni’s 1999 music video Maine Payal Hai Chhankai, of late shared a clip from the song, joking that it was the peak of her career that she has been unable to surpass since.

Adding to this, Himani Shah starred in Falguni Pathak’s Maine Payal Hai Chhankai music video. 'I fear I already peaked' Himani shared the clip with the text, “I fear I already peaked.” She captioned the post, “You guys listen to Falguni Pathak during Navratri. I have receipts.”

Meanwhile, Himani's post made followers nostalgic. A comment read, "Childhood Crush." One more comment read, "mimicking you was my fav thing in childhood and even today." Another comment read, "Baddie before the term was coined." Another fan wrote, “Too good, and I wanted to be you when I was a kid and now i am haha.”

Notably, Himani played one of the key characters in the music video Maine Payal Hai Chhankai. Set against the backdrop of a college arts and puppet show, the video featured Himani as a popular girl who mocks a simple girl who performs puppet shows with Falguni Pathak. The latter was played by Anita Pradhan Kharkar. The video also featured Vivan Bhatena as the male lead. Vivan went on to become a familiar face on television and appeared in films such as Dangal (2016), Judwaa 2 (2017) and Raja the Great (2017).

As per the latest buzz, Beyond her appearance in Falguni Pathak’s hit, Himani was a prominent MTV India VJ and model. She also made a cameo in the 2001 Bollywood movie Yaadein and acted in the 2005 movie Rehle Rehle Na.

In further updates, Today, Himani, who goes by her married name Himani Rajiv Shah, works as a beauty, fashion and luxury lifestyle digital creator based in Mumbai. She has 118K followers on Instagram and is followed by celebrities, including Kareena Kapoor Khan. She is married to Rajiv Shah, the son of prominent Mumbai diamond merchant and movie financier Bharat Shah. The couple are parents to two kids.

On top of that, Falguni Pathak, meanwhile, remains one of India’s most popular voices associated with Navratri and dandiya celebrations. Often called the ‘Dandiya Queen’, she rose to fame in the 1990s with her distinctive Gujarati folk-inspired pop music. Songs such as Maine Payal Hai Chhankai, Chudi Jo Khanki Haathon Mein and Meri Chunar Udd Udd Jaye became chartbusters. Decades later, her songs remain a staple at garba nights.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Frontal nudity gets censor clearance! CBFC retains 2-second adult magazine shot in Doosra; Abhinay Deo calls it an “achievement”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

When asked about the certification Doosra received from the CBFC, Abhinay Deo shared, "It’s an adult-rated movie due to a few scenes. I was there at the censor screening and they asked me, ‘What rating do you want?’. I suggested a U/A rating. They agreed but asked us to cut 3 scenes. I told them, ‘If we can get the movie passed with an A-rating and without a cut, I won’t mind’. They shared, ‘If you are okay with adult-rating, we won’t cut a single shot’. I agreed."

Adding to this, One of the scenes that contributed to the 'A' certification features Tara's father (Ankur Vikal) catching her with an adult magazine during her childhood. The sequence includes a clear, two-second shot of a nude photograph of a woman in the magazine. The CBFC has often been strict about the depiction of nudity on screen, with several films facing cuts over such content. However, in this case, the board allowed the shot to remain intact.

Meanwhile, Abhinay Deo revealed, "Those 2-3 shots, which they wanted to cut, were integral to the movie. One was the magazine shot. Then, we had a reference where we touched upon the Babri Masjid episode. They told me, ‘ Thoda kam kar do , change kar do’ . I confessed that I didn’t want to touch the movie."

Notably, Was Abhinay Deo apprehensive about losing out on the under-18 audience because of the adult certification? He replied, "No, because this is not a movie for teenagers to watch, though it is relevant to them."
As per the latest buzz, Doosra is scheduled to rollout in cinemas on October 23.

title: Ajay Devgn’s team clarifies on partial demolition of Juhu property, confirms BMC-required changes have been made
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Ajay Devgn’s team has issued a clarification after reports emerged that the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation ( BMC ) had partially demolished a property owned by the star in Juhu, Mumbai.

Adding to this, Ajay Devgn’s team issued clarification on partial demolition of Juhu property. ‘We are duly complying with all applicable BMC rules’ Ajay’s team has now issued a statement clarifying that the property in question is not the star’s residence but a separate property that has been rented out.

Meanwhile, The statement read, “We would like to clarify that the property in question is not Ajay Devgn’s residence, but a separate property that has been rented out. We have applied to the BMC for the requisite permissions in respect of one of our properties and are duly complying with all applicable BMC rules, regulations and guidelines. The necessary changes, alterations and modifications, as required by the BMC, have been carried out.”

Notably, According to a report by Hindustan Times , the property, measuring approximately 7,802 square feet, is located in Kapol Co-operative Housing Society and is owned by Ajay and his mother, Veena Devgn.

As per the latest buzz, The BMC’s K/West ward had issued a notice under Section 354A of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act on September 10, 2026, alleging unauthorised additions and alterations at the property. The notice directed the owners to immediately stop the work and produce the requisite permissions within 24 hours. It also warned that the construction could otherwise be demolished at their risk and cost.

In further updates, In a speaking order dated October 6, the designated officer rejected the owners’ reply, stating that no documents establishing the legality of the construction or permissions from the competent authority had been submitted. Consequently, the civic body treated the work as unauthorised and directed its immediate removal.

On top of that, Ajay Devgn is currently enjoying the box-office success of Drishyam 3, the latest instalment in his popular thriller franchise. The movie has as per reports collected ₹ 336.55 crore rupees in India net collections within 16 days of its rollout and crossed the ₹ 500 crore rupees mark in worldwide gross collections. It also recorded the biggest opening of the star’s career.

The star has several projects lined up, including Rohit Shetty’s Golmaal 5. He is also set to feature in Ranger, an soon-to-release action-adventure movie directed by Jagan Shakti and produced by Luv Ranjan, Ankur Garg, Ajay Devgn and Anand Pandit. The movie will feature Sanjay Dutt as the antagonist. Ajay also has Chauhaan, directed by Neeraj Yadav, in his soon-to-release lineup.

Misuse of artificial intelligence has raised concerns for people across the world, especially celebrities, with cases of deepfakes, manipulated videos, and other forms of identity misuse through such technology. There has been an increasing number of actors filing lawsuits over such misuse of their identities. The latest addition to that list is star Neha Sharma , who has taken a stand against it and warned those who are creating AI-generated content using her face and likeness.

Adding to this, Neha Sharma has become the latest star to warn about legal action against the deepfakes of her circulating online. No one should assume that hiding behind a fake account or the use of AI will protect them from accountability.

In further updates, Neha is among several Indian celebrities who have spoken about deepfakes. On top of that, One of the biggest turning points in India's deepfake debate came after Rashmika Mandanna reacted to a manipulated video that went widely shared online. title: Women's groups protest outside Delhi Police headquarters against alleged sexual violence during anti-SIR stir
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Women's organisations on Saturday organised a protest march towards the Delhi Police headquarters over alleged sexual violence by police personnel during the anti-CEC protests, led by the Cockroach Janta Party, in Delhi.

Adding to this, Women's groups protesting outside Delhi Police headquarters, Ashoka Road. (Instagram/@sfidelhi.official) All India Democratic Women’s Association (AIDWA), National Federation of Indian Women (NFIW), All India Mahila Sanskritik Sangathan (AIMSS), All India Progressive Women’s Association (AIPWA) and ALIFA (All India Feminist Alliance) participated in the march along with several other women and student groups like Collective and SFI.

Meanwhile, In a video shared by PTI on X, women protesters were heard raising the slogans of “Delhi Police sharam karo (Delhi Police, shame on you)" and “ tod ke rakhdo vo samaaj, naari jisme bandhi hai aaj (break apart the society that keeps its women shackled)".

Notably, The protesters assembled near Gurudwara Bangla Sahib and marched towards the Delhi Police headquarters to submit a memorandum seeking accountability for the alleged sexual and gender-based violence against demonstrators, news agency PTI reported.

As per the latest buzz, In a joint official statement shared on Facebook, the organisations shared, videos, photographs and personal testimonies had documented alleged sexual harassment and physical violence against women, transgender and non-binary protesters during police action since July 20, with reports increasing from October 2.

In further updates, They also referred to footage that allegedly showed male police personnel assaulting women demonstrators and claimed that incidents of sexual violence had taken place inside police buses and detention centres.

On top of that, “These deliberate actions by the authorities are nothing but misogynistic attempts to silence women's voices and reveal a larger intent to push us out of politics and public life," they alleged.

Delhi ACP, Vivek Bhagat, one of the accused, later alleged that the woman journalist made casteist remarks against him. No FIR has been filed against him while a man from Haryana was arrested for allegedly sharing a fabricated video that falsely showed the officer misbehaving with the woman journalist.

title: Yash confirms Ramayana’s ₹4,000 crore budget for both parts, asks fans to speak about the film with pride
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

At the latest trailer launch event for Ramayana in Bengaluru, Yash addressed the much-discussed ₹ 4,000 crore rupees budget of the movie franchise. The star, who plays Ravana in the soon-to-release epic, is also one of the producers of the movie alongside Namit Malhotra . At the event, Yash verified that the combined budget for both parts of Ramayana is ₹ 4,000 crore rupees.

Adding to this, Yash plays the role of Ravana in Ramayana. ‘Both the movies combined is definitely ₹ 4,000 crore rupees’ As reported by The Hindu, Yash addressed Namit Malhotra’s earlier statement about the budget of the Ramayana duology, which had sparked considerable discussion on social media.

Meanwhile, “I know that Namit's statement went widely shared on social media. In India, there is a problem. People don't like it when you talk confidently. That's what happened with Namit's statement. But in the West, it's the total opposite. If you tell them we have made a good movie in a humble manner, they will dismiss our movie as a small project. That's exactly why Namit has confidently shared that this movie is mounted on ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. We need to prove the strength of the Indian movie industry to the global market,” Yash shared.

Notably, He added, “Ramayana is a two-part project, and the budget for both the movies combined is definitely ₹ 4,000 crore rupees. The budget includes post-production and promotional expenses as well.”

As per the latest buzz, At the event, Yash also thanked his followers for their continued support, even as his soon-to-release movie Toxic received mixed reviews. He assured them that he would strive to deliver an outstanding performance in Ramayana and shared they would be able to speak about the movie with pride.

In further updates, The star also spoke about the ambition behind Ramayana and how they want the movie to reach global audience. He concluded his address by asking the people of Karnataka to bless and support his soon-to-release films.

On top of that, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the Hindu epic. The ambitious project features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana and Sunny Deol as Hanuman. The movie also stars Ravi Dubey, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan and Lara Dutta.
The movie's first instalment is scheduled for a Diwali 2026 rollout (November 5), with the second part planned for Diwali 2027.

Adding to this, Set in the 1980s, the series follows a fictional kingdom shaped by generations of women who have built, governed and protected Pernuru. Written and directed by Dharmaraj Shetty, Akka marks his directorial debut. The cast also includes Tanvi Azmi.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the teaser rollout, Keerthy Suresh shared, “The love I receive from the audience every year makes this day incredibly meaningful, and being able to celebrate it by unveiling the teaser of Akka, a project so close to my heart, feels truly special.”

Notably, Describing her character, the star added, “Bhavani is one of the most unique and memorable characters I have had the opportunity to play. It was lovely working with Radhika. Our characters bring such compelling dynamics to the story and the interplay between them adds an intriguing edge to the narrative.”

As per the latest buzz, Akka also marks Keerthy’s first series with Netflix and YRF Entertainment. Explaining what drew her to the project, she shared, “What drew me to this project was the distinctiveness of its story and the world it inhabits. I am looking forward to audiences immersing themselves in this world and discovering the many facets of Bhavani as her story unfolds.”

In further updates, Radhika Apte, who plays Rudra, spoke about the character’s motivations and the story’s central conflicts. “Rudra is a fascinating character, driven by her own convictions and an instinct to challenge the world around her. What drew me to the series was the complexity of its characters and the tensions that emerge from their differing perspectives,” she shared.

On top of that, The star also noted that the teaser and date announcement coinciding with Keerthy’s birthday made the occasion special. “It's wonderful that the date announcement and the teaser drop of Akka has coincided with Keerthy's birthday. I am sure it is going to be lucky for us,” she added.

Radhika, who has worked with Netflix on several projects, also spoke about collaborating with YRF Entertainment. “Collaborating with YRF Entertainment on a story with such layered characters has been a rewarding experience, and I look forward to audiences discovering Rudra and the many dimensions of her journey,” she shared.

title: Nayyi Navelli box office collection day 1: Yami Gautam's mythological film collects ₹3 crore, fails to surpass Article 370 opening day haul
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nayyi Navelli ticket-window earnings day 1: Yami Gautam in a still from the movie. Nayyi Navelli ticket-window report Nayyi Navelli brings a fantasy entertainer to the big screen, where folklore meets unexpected twists, quirky characters and larger-than-life entertainment. The latest update from Sacnilk states that the movie has collected ₹ 3.25 crore rupees. All eyes are on how the movie performs over the next two days to manage a good opening weekend haul.

Adding to this, Nayyi Navelli has performed better than Rajkummar Rao's Prahaar, which collected ₹ 2.35 crore rupees on its opening day. However, the movie failed to beat the opening day haul of Yami's 2024 rollout Article 370, which had managed ₹ 5.90 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, Set in Meerut, it revolves around a man who accuses his bhabhi (played by Yami) of being a witch, even while her husband and in-laws are fond of her. One day, her husband transforms into a monster, and we are told that it is all linked to Kaal Sheel, a mysterious stone dating back to the Treta Yuga. What follows is a heavy blend of mythology with humour.

Notably, Directed by Balaji Mohan and written by Himanshu Sharma and Divy Nidhi Sharma, the movie also stars Addinath M Kothare, Anurag Thakur, Sunita Rajwar, Mita Vashisht, Aaditya Kulshreshth, Susmita Mukherjee and Pratiek Pachori in pivotal roles. Produced by Aanand L Rai and Himanshu Sharma, the movie features music by G V Prakash Kumar.

As per the latest buzz, An excerpt from the HT review of Nayyi Navelli read, “Nayyi Navelli is a movie that mistakes excess for entertainment and confusion for complexity. Its basic storyline offers enough scope for a blend of mythology and comedy, but the execution fails to do justice to the ideas. The screenplay needed sharper writing, yet it keeps piling on subplots and eccentric characters, hoping that something will eventually click. Yami tries to hold things together, but even her performance cannot compensate for the narrative's shortcomings. 'Nayyi Navelli' may mean something new, but there is precious little that's fresh about the movie itself.”

title: Kriti Sanon approaches Delhi High Court seeking protection against AI-generated impersonation, unauthorised use of identity
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The matter came up before a single-judge Bench of Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav. During the hearing, the court asked Kriti's counsel to place on record relevant judgments, research papers and other material concerning the legal questions surrounding personality rights.

Adding to this, The High Court indicated that it would pass a comprehensive order after examining the judgments and research material submitted by the star's legal team. The matter has now been listed for further hearing on October 29.

Meanwhile, Kriti's plea comes at a time when the unauthorised use of celebrities' identities through digital platforms has become an increasingly prominent legal issue. Apart from the unauthorised commercial use of names and images, courts are also dealing with cases involving AI-generated content, deepfakes, digital impersonation and fake endorsements.

Notably, Personality and publicity rights generally seek to protect aspects of an individual's identity from being commercially exploited or represented without authorisation. The growing use of generative AI has added another layer to these disputes, as digitally created images, videos and other content can closely imitate public figures.

title: Prahaar box office collection day 1: Rajkummar Rao's film collects ₹2.35 crore; fails to beat Mr and Mrs Mahi, Bhool Chuk Maaf
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Rajkummar Rao’s latest outing, Prahaar : The Ujjwal Nikam Story, has opened to a lukewarm response at the ticket-window. The courtroom drama, based on the life of veteran public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam and the trial that led to the hanging of Ajmal Kasab, was rolled out in theatres on Friday. Here’s a look at the movie’s opening-day performance.

Adding to this, Prahaar ticket-window earnings day 1: Rajkummar Rao's movie has collected ₹2.35 crore rupees. Prahaar ticket-window earnings day 1 According to the trade website Sacnilk, Prahaar: The Ujjwal Nikam Story opened with ₹ 2.35 crore rupees in net collections in India, while its gross collection stood at ₹ 2.77 crore rupees. The movie had 4,133 shows across the country and recorded an average occupancy of 13% throughout the day. In terms of worldwide collections, the movie grossed ₹ 0.75 Cr, pushing its total worldwide gross to ₹ 3.52 Cr.

Meanwhile, In the National Capital Region (NCR), the movie had 615 shows, with an average occupancy of 10%. Mumbai recorded 411 shows and 20% occupancy, while Ahmedabad had 283 shows with an average occupancy of 7%.

Notably, With an opening-day collection of ₹ 2.35 crore rupees, Prahaar ranks among the lower openers of Rajkummar Rao’s career. His biggest opener remains Stree 2, which collected ₹ 51.80 crore rupees on its opening day in 2024.

As per the latest buzz, The movie has surpassed the opening-day collections of Srikanth and Badhaai Do, which collected ₹ 2.25 crore rupees and ₹ 1.65 crore rupees, respectively. However, it failed to match the openings of several other Rajkummar's films, including Roohi ( ₹ 2.90 crore rupees), Vicky Vidya Ka Woh Wala Video ( ₹ 5.50 crore rupees), Mr & Mrs Mahi ( ₹ 6.75 crore rupees) and Bhool Chuk Maaf ( ₹ 7 crore rupees).

In further updates, Hindustan Times’ Rishabh Suri gave the movie three stars. In his review, he wrote, “Overall, Prahaar has a story that should have been difficult to look away from, yet it occasionally tests your patience with its own digressions. The 26/11 attack remains one of the darkest scars on our nation's memory. A movie about Ujjwal Nikam had the opportunity to capture the fight for justice with the emotional weight it deserved. Instead, it gets caught between a courtroom drama and a family saga, losing some of its grip on both in the process. And yet, there is enough here to keep the movie from becoming a missed opportunity altogether."

On top of that, Prahaar: The Ujjwal Nikam Story is a courtroom drama based on the life and career of Ujjwal Nikam, the veteran public prosecutor. He played a key role in the prosecution of Ajmal Kasab, the lone surviving terrorist captured during the 26/11 terror attacks, who was later convicted and hanged.
The movie stars Rajkummar Rao as Nikam. It is directed by Avinash Arun and produced by Dinesh Vijan.

title: Prakash Raj says anti-CEC protests will continue despite crackdown: 'There is Gandhi's blood in us'
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Star-activist Prakash Raj shared peaceful protests against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls would continue across the country despite attempts to "suppress" them.

title: Heavy security deployment continues across central Delhi a day after ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Heavy security deployment continued across central Delhi on Saturday, with barricades at Jantar Mantar and additional personnel outside the Delhi Police and Election Commission of India headquarters amid the possibility of fresh protests by left-wing organisations, a day after nearly 2,000 people gathered in and around Connaught Place for the “Lehra Do Tiranga” protest. No major protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) or the Congress party have been revealed so far in the city.

Adding to this, Heavy security deployment continued across central Delhi on Saturday (AFP) Barricades remain in place at Jantar Mantar, which has been de-notified as a designated protest site, and security personnel are manning all three entry and exit points, near the Ashoka Road roundabout and along Tolstoy Marg and Sansad Marg.

Meanwhile, Additional barricades have been put up on Ashoka Road and Jai Singh Road to prevent crowding, as gatherings are prohibited across the New Delhi area under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), an officer aware of the matter shared.

Notably, Security has also been stepped up outside the Delhi Police headquarters and the Election Commission of India headquarters following information that some left-wing organisations may hold a women’s march outside the police headquarters, alleging sexual violence by police during the protests.

As per the latest buzz, “Through our intelligence branch officials, we have learnt that some left groups have planned a march outside the police headquarters later in the morning. Since no permission has been given to anyone to hold protests in the New Delhi area, no gathering will be allowed anywhere in central Delhi. Our security arrangements are in place to handle any flash protest,” the officer added.

In further updates, A senior police officer shared that more than 200 companies of central armed paramilitary forces (CAPFs), comprising nearly 20,000 men and women, are available with the Delhi Police to handle protests across Delhi. The largest deployments of the CAPFs have been made in central Delhi, particularly in and around Jantar Mantar, Sansad Marg, the Election Commission headquarters and Connaught Place, as well as outside the residences of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and other key ministers. Nearly 10,000 Delhi Police personnel have also been kept in reserve to deal with demonstrations and marches in the city, the officers shared.

On top of that, On Friday evening, nearly 2,000 people gathered in and around Connaught Place for the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) “Lehra Do Tiranga” protest, scheduled to be held at Central Park at 5 pm. As police permission was not granted for the protest, Delhi Police and CAPF personnel were deployed in large numbers in Connaught Place and its adjoining areas from Thursday. By Friday noon, hundreds of personnel had taken over Central Park and closed all its access gates to ensure nobody entered the park.

Outside the park, nearly 200 personnel, particularly from the CAPFs, formed a human chain around it as protesters in small groups began marching around Connaught Place’s inner circle after 5 pm. Senior police officers also conducted flag marches along the pavements and restricted movement near the site, including that of journalists. By 7.30 pm, police dispersed protesters from the Connaught Place area. Nearly 150 people were detained from the area, Mandi House and Janpath by 9 pm and were later rolled out.

title: ‘Can you give some research paper?’: Delhi High Court asks Kriti Sanon legal clarity in personality rights protection case
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Kriti Sanon has approached the Delhi High Court seeking protection of her personality rights, with the court on Friday calling for a broader examination of the legal principles governing such claims amid a rise in similar cases.

Adding to this, Kriti Sanon approached the Delhi High Court over protection of her personality rights. (AFP) Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav asked advocate Pravin Anand, appearing for Sanon, to prepare a comprehensive compilation of judgments and research material on personality rights, including the extent of protection available and the jurisdiction of the High Court’s Intellectual Property Division (IPD) to deal with such disputes.

Meanwhile, Observing that such matters are frequently brought before the court, the judge shared the legal issues required a broader examination beyond the facts of the present case. The court asked Kriti 's counsel to explain the contours of personality rights, the attributes of an individual that may receive legal protection and whether such disputes fall within the purview of the IPD.

Notably, Her lawyer, Anand, submitted that personality rights could extend to an individual’s name, voice, face, image, photographs and videos. He also pointed to the commercial use of a person’s identity without their consent or authorisation as an issue arising in such cases. Seeking assistance on the subject, Justice Kaurav asked the counsel to place relevant judicial precedents and research before the court.

As per the latest buzz, “Can you give me some research paper? Please give a compilation. Give me judgments and your understanding regarding personality rights,” the court observed, adding that it would consider passing a comprehensive order after examining the material. Anand told the court that the compilation would be filed during the day and submitted that no jurisdictional issue arose in Kriti's case. The matter has been listed for further hearing on October 29.

In further updates, The proceedings come against the backdrop of an increasing number of petitions concerning personality rights filed by actors, sportspersons and other public figures before the Delhi High Court. Such cases commonly involve allegations of unauthorised use of names, photographs, likenesses, voices and other identifiable aspects of a person’s identity, particularly for commercial purposes.

On top of that, The court has previously dealt with personality rights claims involving several prominent personalities, including actors Kangana Ranaut , Tabu and Vijay Deverakonda , cricketers Abhishek Sharma and Yuvraj Singh, Congress leader Shashi Tharoor and Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan.

The growing use of digital platforms and artificial intelligence has further complicated the issue, particularly in cases involving allegedly unauthorised digital reproductions, impersonation, deepfakes and the use of a public figure’s identity to promote products or services.

title: PCI sets out dos and don’ts for journalists covering protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Press Council of India (PCI) has issued guidelines for journalists covering protests and demonstrations, emphasising professional neutrality, crowd safety, ethical reporting and coordination between newsrooms and reporters in the field.

Adding to this, Students from the All India Students’ Association (AISA) and other student organisations detained by Delhi Police during the protest Tiranga march at Connaught Place on Friday. (Sanjeev Verma/Hindustan Times) The guidelines, adopted at the council’s meeting on October 14, were dated Thursday, according to a press rollout dated October 15. They seek to facilitate effective media coverage of protests while protecting journalists and promoting responsible reporting.

Meanwhile, PCI is a statutory, quasi-judicial body established under the Press Council Act, 1978. Its jurisdiction covers print media, including newspapers and news agencies, but does not extend to television, radio or internet-based digital news platforms.

Notably, The guidelines advise journalists to carry valid identity cards issued by their media organisations or applicable Press Information Bureau (PIB) or Directorate of Information and Publicity (DIP) accreditation, and keep their press identification visible. They should also secure identity cards and lanyards to prevent them from getting caught during crowd movement or confrontations.

As per the latest buzz, Emphasising professional neutrality, the council has advised journalists against participating in demonstrations, taking sides, provoking confrontations or interfering with protesters, counter-protesters or police. Media personnel should remain respectful, follow police orders and comply with lawful instructions issued for immediate safety, while calmly asserting their press status when necessary.

In further updates, On crowd safety, journalists have been advised to maintain a reasonable distance from confrontations, particularly when tensions escalate or police action is anticipated. They should avoid attaching cameras or recording equipment to police barricades, vehicles or other equipment in ways that obstruct movement or cause damage. The guidelines also call for careful movement through crowds and continuous assessment of potential risks.

On top of that, The council has stressed situational awareness and escape planning. Journalists should monitor changes in crowd behaviour, identify nearby exits, open streets and safe locations, and adjust escape routes as conditions change. In areas affected by smoke or tear gas, they should use visible landmarks and safe routes to exit without moving deeper into the crowd.

The guidelines recommend carrying an emergency kit containing basic first-aid supplies, essential medication, drinking water, high-protein snacks, a flashlight, a washcloth or hand towel, and eye protection or goggles. Protective headgear and body armour may be considered depending on the assessed threat. Journalists have also been cautioned against touching or moving tear-gas canisters, flash-bang devices or smoke grenades.

title: BJP, Oppn trade barbs over protests against CEC, SIR
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Lucknow/New Delhi: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday attacked the Opposition Congress over protests against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, accusing it of trying to seize power by spreading anarchy, even as the party hit back, saying it wanted to defeat the BJP through democratic means and not extra-constitutional methods.

Adding to this, India News “This fight is not for electoral reforms, not for SIR, not against Gyanesh Kumar, not for bright future of youth. It is a conspiracy to grab power. In democracy there is no licence to spread anarchy and attack constitutional institutions,” Singh shared while addressing a press conference in Lucknow.

Meanwhile, Congress MP Pawan Khera rejected the allegations, accusing the BJP of treating protests as anti-national when it faced public criticism. “The BJP is not used to democracy when it is on the receiving end of it. When it has to face the heat of democracy, answer questions and confront protests, democracy suddenly begins to look like treason and anti-national activity to them,” he shared.

Notably, Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets seeking Kumar’s removal and the scrapping of SIR, even as authorities ordered Metro closures, Internet shutdowns, imposed prohibitory orders and deployed 40,000 security personnel to turn Delhi into a virtual fortress. Many protesters were dragged, manhandled and detained as the ruling BJP accused the Opposition of trying to deflect attention from its electoral failures.

As per the latest buzz, Singh accused the Congress and its allies of seeking a change of government along the lines of Bangladesh, saying they were using the energy of young people to spread anarchy and undermine democratic institutions.

In further updates, “It appears that the Congress and its political allies, directly and through their supporting organisations, are trying to use the energy of the youth to fuel political confrontation and spread anarchy instead of channelling it towards constructive work and nation-building,” he shared. “The youth of the country are being made pawns in the politics of anarchy,” he added.

On top of that, “They openly say at press conferences that they have drawn inspiration from Bangladesh for regime change, while another speaks openly about bringing down the government. This makes it clear that their only agenda is to dismantle democratic institutions and set the country on fire,” he shared, referring to the uprising in Bangladesh in 2024 that toppled the Sheikh Hasina government.

Khera shared the Opposition wanted to change the government through elections, citing the change of government in 1977 after the Emergency. “How does regime change happen in a democracy like India? Through elections. Changing the regime through elections is precisely the Opposition’s objective,” he shared.

title: CJP protest LIVE: Dipke produced before Delhi Magistrate for bail hearing at Mandir Marg Police Station
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Dipke had been detained on Friday ahead of the ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march called by the CJP in Central Park in Connaught Place. ...Read More

title: SC warns of ‘constitutional tort’ over protest-related hardship to traders, workers
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Friday warned that it could invoke its constitutional tort jurisdiction to award compensation if protests in Delhi disproportionately affect traders and daily-wage earners, expressing concern over the hardship faced by small businesses during the festive season.

Adding to this, A view CP Market during the in a Tiranga March on Friday. (RAJ K RAJ /HT PHOTO) A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi made the observations while hearing a plea raising concerns over the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) call for a gathering at Central Park in Connaught Place on Friday evening. The court hoped that “better sense will prevail” and that the competing interests of protesters, traders and authorities would be balanced.

Meanwhile, “If there is loss of business, if it is unlawful to your clients, we will exercise our powers under constitutional tort jurisdiction. Let’s cross that bridge when it comes,” justice Bagchi told advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai, who mentioned the petition on behalf of a traders’ association.

Notably, The observations came a day after the Delhi High Court recorded an assurance from Delhi Police that it would take “all possible measures under the law” to regulate the proposed gathering and address concerns over disruption to business and movement around Connaught Place.

As per the latest buzz, Dehadrai told the Supreme Court that the protest could cause substantial losses to traders, particularly during the festive season, when businesses depend on higher sales for a significant share of their annual earnings. He claimed that disruption around Connaught Place was causing losses of more than ₹ 250 crore rupees a day.

In further updates, Initially indicating that the matter would not be taken up immediately, CJI Kant shared, “This is also related to protest. It can wait till October 26.” Justice Bagchi pointed out that the Delhi High Court had heard a similar petition on Thursday.

On top of that, When counsel insisted that the Supreme Court plea raised distinct concerns, the judge shared the competing claims of protesters, traders and law enforcement agencies had to be considered together. “Someone wants to protest, someone wants to sell moongfali (peanuts), someone wants to maintain law and order. All are there before us. We can hear it after a week,” he shared.

The CJI expressed concern over the economic vulnerability of small traders and their families during the festive period. “We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers, they earn their livelihood during these days. We know the hardship, difficulty and crises entire families face,” he shared.

title: Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora among 150 detained in Delhi; Oppn slams police action amid anti-CEC protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police personnel at Abhijeet Dipke's door, his detention on the way to Connaught Place (CP) and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s claim that he was taken to an “undisclosed” location - the outfit's ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ call was marked by police action and a big crowd in central Delhi.

Adding to this, Abhijeet Dipke and Neha Bora were detained on their way to the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' rally in Delhi on Friday. At least 150 people were detained around Janpath Road, CP and Mandi House in Delhi. AISA activist Neha Bora was also among those picked up. As the day came to a close, both Dipke and Bora's teams claimed that they had no information on their whereabouts.

Meanwhile, Several Opposition leaders, including Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal and MK Stalin backed Dipke and Bora and called the situation in Delhi an “undeclared emergency”. The former Tamil Nadu chief minister also raised questions about their whereabouts after detention.
Notably, Earlier in the day, the CJP founder was served a notice by the Delhi Police and was asked not to join the rally. The notice cited prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS.

As per the latest buzz, The notice contended that Connaught Place was not a “notified protest site” as it asked Dipke not to hold the march. It also shared that the CJP founder must refrain from infringing on the rights of other citizens.

In further updates, “Connaught Place is not a notified protest site and that demonstrations may be held at designated venues, subject to the necessary permission being sought and granted," a part of the notice read.

On top of that, The notice also pointed to CP being a hub for businesses and housing several prominent restaurants and outlets. “It (CP) houses a dense concentration of showrooms, restaurants, hotels, banks, offices and street vendors, so any disruption, particularly during evening and weekend hours, as well as the peak festival season, directly affects the livelihood of traders and their employees. Over 15 lakh traders and their employees depend on its peaceful and orderly functioning for the exercise of their fundamental right,” the notice read.
The notice was personally handed to Abhijeet Dipke by the Delhi Police personnel at NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande's residence.

title: 'Bhaag Neha Bhaag, Jantar Mantar Chalo': Delhi protests inspire online games where players take on roles of protesters, cops
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Protests at Jantar Mantar are now inspiring online gaming experiences. Developers have created free online games inspired by the demonstrations, giving players virtual roles as protesters and police personnel in challenges involving crowds, barricades and detentions.

Adding to this, A series of free video games inspired by demonstrations at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar allows players to recreate aspects of the protests. (bhaagnehabhaag.netlify.app/https://mantarjantar.com/) From ‘ Jantar Mantar Chalo’, which lets players choose between protesters and police personnel, to ‘Bhaag Neha Bhaag’, inspired by AISA national president Neha Bora ’s attempts to reach the protest site, the games draw on recent political developments and the scenes that unfolded on the streets of the national capital.

Meanwhile, Another game, ‘Jantar Mantar to Jail’, features Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) members Abhijeet Dipke , Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Players must dodge falling jail bars and police personnel while collecting coins representing “accountability” and “democracy”.
Notably, The games allows users to participate in virtual versions of events that have attracted attention online.

As per the latest buzz, Inspired by the protests is ‘Bhaag Neha Bhaag’, created by 30-year-old screenwriter and filmmaker Anav Nayar. He co-founded Wizloop Studios with his brother, Akshay Nayar, with the company focusing on content strategy, intellectual property for brands and the creative use of AI, PTI reported.
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Anav Nayar (@anavnayar)
On top of that, Nayar shared the idea came from following Neha Bora’s attempts to reach Jantar Mantar and her repeated detentions.

“We were following how Neha Bora and other protesters were trying to reach Jantar Mantar. They were detained but the very next day, they were back at the spot. “My brother Akshay asked me how they were managing to do it, and that got me thinking about creating a game around it,” Nayar told PTI.

title: The best ending for Drishyam is NO Drishyam 4. Why Ajay Devgn and Abhishek Pathak are RIGHT to end the blockbuster franchise
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The phenomenal success of Drishyam The Conclusion has once again demonstrated the extraordinary popularity of Ajay Devgn's Vijay Salgaonkar. Rolled out on October 2, the suspense thriller has emerged as one of the biggest Bollywood successes of 2026, crossing the Rs. 500 crore rupees mark at the worldwide ticket-window. At a time when even star-studded entertainers are struggling to justify their budgets, Drishyam The Conclusion has proved that an engaging story, memorable characters and clever writing can still bring audiences to cinemas in huge numbers.

Adding to this, Going by conventional Bollywood logic, this should be the perfect opportunity to announce Drishyam 4 . After all, why would any producer willingly discontinue a franchise capable of generating hundreds of crores?

Meanwhile, Yet, director Abhishek Pathak has made it clear that the journey of Vijay Salgaonkar has reached its destination and that there are no plans for another instalment. It is a decision that deserves to be celebrated, not questioned. Because, sometimes, the smartest decision a filmmaker can make is to walk away from a goldmine. The Rs. 500 crore rupees temptation

Notably, Let's face it. If Drishyam 4 were revealed tomorrow, the trade would undoubtedly sit up and take notice. The combination of Ajay Devgn, Vijay Salgaonkar, October 2 and the promise of another mind-bending climax would be sufficient to generate enormous curiosity.
As per the latest buzz, The producers already have something that filmmakers spend years trying to create: an established franchise with tremendous audience goodwill.

In further updates, The first Drishyam (2015) gradually acquired a cult following, while Drishyam 2 (2022) emerged as a major theatrical success at a time when the Hindi movie industry desperately needed reassurance that audiences were willing to return to cinemas. Drishyam The Conclusion has taken the franchise's commercial potential to an entirely different level.
On top of that, Therefore, commercially speaking, making another instalment might appear to be a no-brainer.

But cinema cannot always be reduced to a balance sheet. There is a difference between a movie making money because it has a compelling story and a movie being made simply because there is money to be collected.

title: Subhash Ghai says actors of this generation prioritise money over art, recalls how actors took 40% fees in his films
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Subhash Ghai has directed some of the most successful films in the 1980s and 90s, including Khalnayak, Hero, Pardes and Taal. The filmmaker has now reacted to how actors today prioritise money over their craft. In an interview with Screen, the filmmaker spoke about the change that has taken place in the industry.

Adding to this, Filmmaker Subhash Ghai spoke about the changing business of cinema. (PTI Photo) (PTI11_26_2024_000410B) (PTI) What Subhash Ghai shared The director shared, “Commerce has taken over. Today, the children want to earn more money, and it’s less about the art. During our time, the actors wanted to be artistes, and thought money will eventually come. Nobody would wait for the money. They would sign a movie based on the director, the story and the character. Most of the stars in my movies have taken only 40 per cent of the price because they were interested in the character and the story.”

Meanwhile, He added, "Today, if you ask any star to take only 40 per cent fees, four of their managers will intervene, and 3 PRs will come in together to endorse the star as a star. Today, there are various other means of earning for actors rather than just movies. But again, they are seasonal; the craze dies down after 3-4 years. Then they are out of the picture, and somebody else walks in.”

Notably, On Koffee with Karan Season 9, even Salman Khan brought out this issue in the movie industry. We want to get out of our houses and do good work. Sometimes, it turns out right, sometimes it does not.”

title: Press Council of India issues guidelines for journalists covering protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Press Council of India (PCI), a statutory and quasi-judicial body meant to preserve press freedom, has issued guidelines for journalists covering protests, emphasising professional conduct, crowd safety, ethical reporting and coordination with newsrooms and law enforcement agencies.

Adding to this, Many protesters have been dragged, manhandled and detained. (AP Photo) The guidelines were rolled out on Thursday to “facilitate orderly and effective media coverage of protests” while ensuring the safety of journalists and responsible reporting. They call on journalists to carry valid identity cards issued by their media organisations or applicable Press Information Bureau (PIB)/Directorate of Information and Publicity (DIP) accreditation. They ask journalists to keep their press identification clearly visible while reporting.

Meanwhile, The guidelines were issued against the backdrop of tens of thousands of people taking to the streets seeking chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s removal and the scrapping of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll. The authorities ordered Metro closures, Internet shutdowns, imposed prohibitory orders and deployed 40,000 security personnel to turn Delhi into a virtual fortress.
Notably, Many protesters were dragged, manhandled and detained. On Sunday, at least 12 journalists covering the second day of protests were detained.

As per the latest buzz, The PCI, which has jurisdiction only over print media under the Press Council Act of 1978, has advised journalists to secure their identity cards and lanyards carefully to prevent entanglement during crowd movement or confrontations. It emphasised professional neutrality and asked journalists not to participate in demonstrations, take sides, provoke confrontations or interfere with protesters, counterprotesters or police.

In further updates, The PCI advised media personnel to remain respectful, follow police orders and comply with lawful instructions issued for immediate safety, while calmly asserting their press status when necessary.

On top of that, The PCI asked journalists to maintain a reasonable distance from confrontations, particularly when tensions escalate, or police action is anticipated. It shared they should avoid attaching cameras or recording equipment to police barricades, vehicles, or other equipment in ways that could obstruct movement or cause damage.
The guidelines recommend careful movement through crowds and continuous assessment of potential dangers. They stressed the importance of situational awareness and escape planning.

title: Delhi Police ask Dipke to call off Connaught Place demonstration, say area is not a protest site
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police has prohibited CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke from holding any form of demonstration, procession or rally in the vicinity of Connaught Place, citing the need to protect public safety, traffic movement and the rights of citizens and traders.

Adding to this, A Delhi Police official with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, ahead of the party's 'Lehra Do Tiranga' rally. In a notice served to Dipke on Friday, Delhi Police told CJP founder that “Connaught Place is not a notified protest site and that demonstrations may be held at designated venues, subject to the necessary permission being sought and granted.” It further shared that such an “unlawful assembly” posed a serious risk to public order and infringed on the rights of other citizens.

Meanwhile, A prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is currently in force in the area and any violation could invite action under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and other applicable laws, police told Dipke.
Notably, “Not only has no permission been sought, but any unauthorised public gathering could critically imperil the factors mentioned by the Hon’ble Apex Court,” the notice shared.

As per the latest buzz, Delhi Police shared the event could disrupt traffic and affect businesses, including showrooms, restaurants, hotels, banks, offices and street vendors. Police, in the notice, also warned of possible congestion or a stampede near Rajiv Chowk Metro station, which caters to an average of two lakh commuters daily.

In further updates, “It (CP) houses a dense concentration of showrooms, restaurants, hotels, banks, offices and street vendors, so any disruption, particularly during evening and weekend hours, as well as the peak festival season, directly affects the livelihood of traders and their employees. Over 15 lakh traders and their employees depend on its peaceful and orderly functioning for the exercise of their fundamental right,” the notice read.

On top of that, Delhi Police shared several arterial roads pass through CP, and their obstruction could paralyse traffic across central Delhi. It also cited, in the notice, the area's proximity to Parliament, the Central Secretariat and diplomatic precincts, raising concerns about public order and security.
Police further shared narrow service lanes and older buildings could impede the movement of fire tenders and ambulances, potentially compromising emergency response services.

Adding to this, The TVK joined the INDIA bloc’s protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) leader Thol. Thirumavalavan shared. In further updates, TVK’s participation in the protest follows a series of political engagements with opposition parties in Tamil Nadu. On top of that, The meeting discussed coordinated opposition to the BJP-led Union government and the SIR exercise. The parties also passed resolutions, including one welcoming TVK into the state-level opposition grouping.

title: Nitanshi Goel joins Korean skincare brand Mamonde as its first India brand ambassador
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nitanshi captured the country’s attention with her breakout performance in Laapataa Ladies, winning hearts with her charm and natural screen presence. Now, she is stepping into the world of Korean beauty with Mamonde, a brand that pairs skincare science with the power of flowers. With young Indian consumers increasingly looking to K-beauty for innovative formulations and effective skincare, the partnership brings together a rising young star and a brand looking to make its mark in one of beauty’s most exciting categories.

Adding to this, “India’s beauty consumers are evolving quickly, and the relevance of Korean beauty among young people continues to grow. With Mamonde, we are bringing innovative, benefit-led skincare to India at accessible price points. Nitanshi’s youthful energy and relatability make her the ideal face to introduce Mamonde to the next generation of beauty consumers. This appointment reflects our long-term commitment to building Mamonde into a strong Korean skincare brand in India,” shared Paul Lee, Managing Director & Country Head, Amorepacific India.

Meanwhile, “Mamonde brings together Korean skincare expertise, targeted formulations and a fresh approach to everyday beauty. With Nitanshi on board, we have an opportunity to bring the brand closer to young consumers through campaigns and conversations that feel relevant to them. From discovering products for specific skin concerns to finding new favourites for their everyday routines, we want to make exploring Mamonde an exciting experience for India’s young beauty community,” added Mini Sood Banerjee, Deputy Director, Amorepacific India.

Notably, The partnership also brings Mamonde’s philosophy, ‘Let Your Skin Bloom’, to life. Rooted in the resilience and transformative power of flowers, the philosophy celebrates the idea that beauty is never one-size-fits-all. Just as every flower blooms differently, every individual has unique skin needs. Mamonde encourages consumers to embrace that individuality and discover skincare that works for them.

As per the latest buzz, “I’m really excited to be joining Mamonde as its first brand ambassador in India. What drew me to the brand is how it combines Korean skincare innovation with a message that feels personal. ‘Let Your Skin Bloom’ is something I connect with because everyone’s skin is different, and skincare should be about discovering what makes you feel your best. I can’t wait to introduce more young people to Mamonde and be part of the brand’s journey in India,” shared Nitanshi Goel.

In further updates, Mamonde’s skincare range brings a targeted approach to everyday skin concerns. The Rose HA range, featuring a Serum and Sunscreen, focuses on hydration for a plump-looking, dewy complexion. The Peony BHA range, comprising a Serum and Sunscreen, addresses pore care and excess sebum management while providing UV protection. The range also features the Liquid Mask, a leave-on formula that combines gentle exfoliation with glow-enhancing benefits for an easy addition to everyday skincare routines.

On top of that, With its first brand ambassador now on board, Mamonde is set to introduce more Indian consumers to its take on Korean skincare, with Nitanshi helping bring its ‘Let Your Skin Bloom’ philosophy to life.

title: Nayyi Navelli review: Yami Gautam tries to hold together a fantasy film that thinks big, but barely makes sense
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Cast: Yami Gautam, Addinath Kothare, Sunita Rajwar, Mita Vashisht

Adding to this, The promotional material for Nayyi Navelli had one thing repeatedly mentioned: “Think big!” And so, with plenty of hope, I walked in to watch the movie, only to walk out wondering if the makers themselves had missed the memo.

Meanwhile, Directed by Balaji Mohan and written by Himanshu Sharma, the movie’s narrative is all over the place. Set in Meerut, it revolves around a man who accuses his bhabhi (played by Yami Gautam Dhar ) of being a witch, even while her husband and in-laws are fond of her. One day, her husband transforms into a monster, and we are told that it is all linked to Kaal Sheel, a mysterious stone dating back to the Treta Yuga. What follows is a heavy blend of mythology with humour.

Notably, The biggest problem is the screenplay, which lacks clarity and direction. The movie begins abruptly, leaving the viewer struggling to make sense of the events unfolding on screen. The narrative is further weighed down by a family of eccentric characters, most of whom alternate between delivering random one-liners and breaking into unnecessary shouting. The humour rarely feels organic, while the constant commotion does little to advance the story. At times, the movie feels less like a tightly written screenplay and more like an improvised series of scenes that have been strung together incoherently. The interval point feels like the movie's climax, and not in a good way.

As per the latest buzz, The second half thankfully picks up pace, introducing some interesting backstories that add some depth to the narrative. However, the respite is short lived, as Nayyi Navelli soon falls back into the same trap of excess. The movie struggles with restraint, stretching subplots and comic sequences well beyond their natural length. A track involving the marriage of a much older woman to a younger man, for instance, is given a lot of screen time without adding much to the narrative. If the intention is to extract a laugh or two, well, the sequence proves to be too flat to elicit even a chuckle.

In further updates, Among the performances, it's left to Yami to do the heavy lifting here. And she does well, to an extent. Without a solid story, how much can you expect an star to really perform? She has the presence and the emotional range, just not the material to make them both shine. The rest of the entire cast is strictly okay.
On top of that, The background score by GV Prakash Kumar helps occasionally, but also tends to get a bit loud. And the music, again by him, doesn't stand out.
The story is heavily reliant on VFX, and that is decent.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Designer Suneet Varma showcased his latest collection Kashi at the ongoing Lakme Fashion Week with Laapataa Ladies star Nitanshi Goel turning up as the showstopper.
Adding to this, Varma's collection blended traditional craftsmanship with contemporary glamour in ready-to-wear skirts, draped saris, tops, trousers, dhoti skirts, jackets, and corset tops.
Meanwhile, The designer, who has been a major figure in Indian fashion industry for over three decades, shared he wanted to create contemporary outfits that can be worn globally.
Notably, The collection was inspired by a past trip to Varanasi where he had gone to source textiles.

As per the latest buzz, "It is very old Banaras... One of the last models who walked the ramp, she wore a beautiful cape with tree of life motif. I went to the city some 32-years ago to source textiles, and I made a cape, a similar cape with that tree of life motif. This time when I started with 'Kashi', I took the same artwork from something I had done years ago and built it with a Kashi landscape," he told reporters post show.

In further updates, "For me, it is very nostalgic and beautiful. It is an inspiration because it goes back to the tree of life, it goes back to spirituality, but I also wanted to make it modern," he added.

On top of that, Goel walked the ramp wearing a wine coloured lehenga with a contemporary twist to it. The attire featured an off-shoulder draped top and a mermaid-tail skirt with heavy sequin details all over.
"When I saw his vision, and I sort of envisioned myself in it, all I knew is I am going to feel pretty tonight... I am super grateful, and I love the collection," she added.

title: In tense livestream, Delhi cops ask Abhijeet Dipke to call off CP Tiranga march; Central Park blockade planned
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police shared it is planning to block all entries to Central Park in Connaught Place ahead of the proposed ‘ Lehra Do Tiranga ’ rally by Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke, while allowing traffic and pedestrian movement in the inner and outer circles of CP. Dipke was later detained by Delhi Police while heading towards Connaught Place for the march.

Adding to this, CJP's Abhijeet Dipke has planned to hold a rally to unfold the Tricolour at Central Park in Delhi's CP (Instagram and PTI) A police team has also visited Dipke's place of stay — NCP-SP spokesperson Anish Gawande's residence — to verbally inform him about prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), in force in the New Delhi area, and urge him to call off the march and maintain peace and law and order. Track LIVE updates from Abhijeet Dipke's Tiranga march here
Meanwhile, The police team left the house after serving a notice to Dipke and getting the acknowledgement, a police officer shared.
Notably, CJP livestreamed the tense exchange between Dipke and Delhi Police personnel, in which the former can be heard asking an officer how unfolding the Tricolour is unlawful.

As per the latest buzz, "We are not putting any speaker, we have not shared it is a protest, we are just saying we will unfold the Tricolour, is that now allowed?" Dipke could be seen asking the officer.
In further updates, Citing the communication in the notice, Dipke further asked, "Is Tiranga unlawful?", and got "it is country's pride" as a response from the officer.

On top of that, Abhijeet Dipke proposed “Lehra Do Tiranga” protest march to CP's Central Park on Wednesday amid the standoff with authorities over the arrest of two spokespersons of CJP - Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - for Jantar Mantar trespass.

Saurav Das and its Ashutosh Ranka were detained by the Delhi Police on Tuesday morning after entering Jantar Mantar by jumping the locked gates, a day after the site lost its designated protest venue status.

title: CID's Shivaji Satam recalls Nana Patekar fighting for his pay, stood by him during wife’s cancer battle: ‘Supported me like a real brother’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Shivaji Satam remembered Nana Patekar at a condolence meeting held in his honour. The gathering, titled ‘athvanitle Nana (Nana in our memories), was held at P.L. Deshpande Maharashtra Kala Academy complex in Prabhadevi in Mumbai, where several members of the movie industry came together to remember the star and the impact he had on their lives.

Adding to this, Shivaji Satam gets emotional remembering Nana Patekar, reveals how he stood by him during wife’s cancer battle. Shivaji remembered Nana and it meant looking back at nearly 40 years of friendship, countless personal memories and the support he received from the star at crucial moments in his life. He recalled how Nana encouraged him to take up Hindi films and even stepped in when he felt his friend was not being paid enough.

Meanwhile, Speaking at the prayer meet, Shivaji Satam, known as ACP Pradyuman from CID TV Show, shared, “Nana passed away so suddenly. When I heard the news, I honestly couldn't believe it. I have countless memories with Nana. We had known each other for nearly 40 years, and it was because of him that I found my footing in Hindi cinema. He was the one who pulled me into Hindi films. He convinced me, saying, ‘You should do this. You must do it.’"

Notably, Satam recalled that Nana was instrumental in getting him his first Hindi movie, Yashwant. “My first movie was Yashwant. The producer called me because there was a police officer's role in the movie, but I wasn't ready to take it up at the time. The producer told me that Nana Patekar, my friend, had recommended my name. When I refused, the producer called Nana, who then spoke to me in his own way and convinced me. Eventually, after saying no several times, I agreed," he revealed.

As per the latest buzz, He shared he was initially reluctant to take up the role of a police officer, but Nana personally convinced him to give it a shot. Their conversation did not end with the movie, though. When Nana later learnt how much Satam had been paid, he was upset that his friend had not consulted him before agreeing to the amount. “After the shoot was over, I met Nana again, and he asked me about the payment I had received. When I told him the amount, he got really angry. He shared, ‘You should have asked me at least once!’ He then scolded me, asking why I hadn't consulted him before accepting the payment. After that, he called the producers himself," the star further shared.

In further updates, Satam went on to share how Nana reacted when he learnt about the remuneration his friend had received. Even though Shivaji had asked him not to get involved, Nana was not willing to let the matter go. He wanted to make sure Satam was treated fairly and took it upon himself to speak to the producers.

On top of that, “I had specifically told him not to question the producers or speak to them about it. But Nana wouldn't listen. He made the producers stand for two hours, just like teachers used to make us stand in school. The poor producer stood there without saying a word," he revealed.

Shivaji's memories of Nana were not limited to their work together. One of the most difficult periods came when his wife was diagnosed with cancer while he was shooting for Ghulam-E-Musthafa. Unsure about how he would manage the movie alongside his family’s medical crisis, he considered stepping away from the project. Nana, however, made sure he did not have to deal with everything alone.
