title: Eknath Shinde sees foreign hand in protests, says Rahul-led march to SC was ‘black day’ for democracy
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde on Tuesday accused the Opposition of conspiring with foreign powers to incite civil unrest, claiming that “foreign powers” were backing the Opposition-led protests in Delhi and that the march to the Supreme Court to file a petition on September 12 was a “black day” for democracy.

Adding to this, Mumbai: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde addresses a press conference at his residence in Mumbai on Tuesday (PTI) The Shiv Sena president also claimed that external entities were conspiring to derail India’s economic progress and spread civil unrest.

Meanwhile, Shinde shared the Opposition march to the Supreme Court on Monday was no trivial matter and an attack on the top court. “It was an insult to India’s highest judiciary. And that’s why I condemn this once again, and they should apologise to the 1.4 billion people of India,” he told a media briefing in Mumbai.

Notably, The deputy CM also questioned the motives of opposition leaders who, he shared, had been invoking political upheavals in neighbouring nations. “The Opposition is citing examples of Nepal, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka. Do they want civil unrest in India? If they cannot rule the country, they are looking at avenues to destroy it,” he alleged.

As per the latest buzz, The Shiv Sena leader’s sharp attacks on the Opposition, particularly Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, came a day after thousands of people flooded central Delhi for three hours in protest against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, one of the largest political mobilisations in recent years that followed two days of police crackdown on agitators.

In further updates, Gandhi led the march from the Constitution Club to Bhagwan Das Road and later walked into the Supreme Court to file a petition demanding an independent, time-bound investigation into decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by Kumar and to suspend the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) pending this inquiry. The petition is expected to be heard on Thursday.

On top of that, Shinde shared the Opposition must respect the position of the prime minister and insisted that the protests are detrimental to the country and the opposition wants to destabilise India. “If they can’t rule India, they are looking at avenues to destroy India,” he shared.

The protests are part of a longer string of events that have mounted pressure on chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the controversial special intensive revision – which has already deleted 130 million names from India’s electoral rolls – and other allegations. The developments come after an Indian Express investigation shared election commissioners SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded written dissents and objections at least 14 times between November 2025 and August 2026 and even written to the cabinet secretary. It also alleged that election officials found their access to the ECI software curtailed by the central IT team. ECI shared differing views and observations were a normal part of deliberation and that all its digital platforms operated under strict data security protocols.

title: ‘They forced us all into the vehicle’: Lekha Washington speaks out after Mumbai detention with Imran Khan and Zayn Marie, says she was left bruised
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Lekha Washington has opened up about her detention with partner Imran Khan and star Zayn Marie during a protest in Mumbai on Saturday. In an Instagram post, Lekha described how the three had gone to August Kranti Maidan to check on friends who had been detained, only to find themselves caught up in a tense situation involving the police and media personnel. She alleged that she and Zayn were grabbed by uniformed officers, leaving them with bruises, before the group was taken away in a vehicle. They were rolled out later that day.

Adding to this, Lekha Washington recalls tense Mumbai detention with Imran Khan and Zayn Marie, says they were driven around for hours. Lekha narrates what happened at the protest Lekha shared she, Imran, Zayn Marie, Imran's mother, Nuzhat and a few others reached August Kranti Maidan at around 5 pm on Saturday. Their intention, she explained, was to find out what had happened to friends who had been detained.

Meanwhile, According to her account, there was no gathering at the venue when they arrived, although the area was barricaded and several media personnel were present. Imran was approached by reporters and briefly explained why they were there. “He responded to the questions from the media, saying we have no demands, we are not part of an organisation, we are just individuals,” she wrote.

Notably, Lekha shared the interaction was cut short by loud whistles and the commotion around them, leaving Imran unable to finish what he was saying. “Before he could even finish his sentence, with the weight of the media on one side, loud and incessant whistle-blowing disrupted everything,” she added.

As per the latest buzz, She then described how the situation escalated, alleging that officers grabbed her and Zayn, causing bruises, before forcing everyone into a vehicle. Lekha claimed they were driven around for a couple of hours and were not allowed to take public transport afterwards. “A stream of uniformed persons grabbed both Zayn and me, bruising us. They forced us all into the vehicle and then drove us around for a couple of hours. After that, they did not allow us to take public transport,” she wrote.

In further updates, View this post on Instagram Lekha reflects on privilege In her post, Lekha also pointed out that she and her companions were in a position of privilege, adding that others could be facing much worse circumstances. She acknowledged the Mumbai Police's role in her own experiences and shared she continued to value the force.

On top of that, “It is important to note that we are individuals in a position of privilege and that far worse is being done to others. The Mumbai Police has been a beacon of balance in my personal experience, and I appreciate them deeply. I believe in equality and respect for all, and at some point we must collectively find our voices to speak the truth. Thank you,” she concluded.

Videos and photographs showing Imran, Lekha and Zayn being escorted into a police van began circulating on social media on Saturday. The three later verified that they had been rolled out. Lekha shared a reel that evening to let people know they were safe. She also posted an Instagram Story showing her hugging Imran and Zayn after they returned home.

The video digitally manipulated Janhvi’s appearance in the song Chuttamalle from Devara , depicting her in a sexually explicit manner. Janhvi, Jr NTR and others condemned the video. Shriya Saran on misuse of AI In an interview with News18, Shriya, who has also been a victim of AI abuse, with morphed images of her circulating online, spoke about the issue. She shared, "It’s funny. Sometimes, I don’t even know if it’s me. They change the size of your b**s, suddenly the cape that you were wearing is gone or your a* looks bigger. You’ve to take it with a pinch of salt. Having shared that, it’s annoying and it’s not right."

Meanwhile, She added, "While AI has a lot to give us and a lot to help us with, there’s also a lot it can change for us. It can lead to things that can be dangerous. I think that applies to every technology. With time, we’ve to either learn to live with it or deal with it."

Notably, Earlier this week, an AI-morphed video featuring Janhvi and Jr NTR in the Chuttamalle song from their 2024 movie Devara sparked a massive debate online. Janhvi posted on Instagram to condemn the ‘criminal misuse’ of AI to objectify women, describing the video as ‘deeply violating’ and ‘bordering on sexual assault’. title: Left protestors clash with police in Patna amid protest march against SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Hundreds of students and youths under the banner of All India Students Association (AISA) and Revolutionary Youth Association (RYA) had a scuffle with police at Patna's main centre, Dak Bungalow roundabout, on Tuesday afternoon.

Adding to this, Protesters breach the security barricades during the All India Students' Association (AISA)- and Revolutionary Youth Association (RYA)-led Lok Bhawan March demanding the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls, in Patna on Tuesday. (ANI) The scuffle broke out after the students were stopped by the police during a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
Meanwhile, AISA serves as the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist–Leninist) Liberation, while RYA is the party's youth wing.

Notably, The situation is tense, with police trying to stop the protestors from moving towards Lok Bhawan amid heavy deployment of police personnel, reports shared. The protestors continue to block the Dak Bungalow roundabout, leading to heavy jams on arterial roads in central Patna .

As per the latest buzz, Police had already detained two dozen protesters soon after the protest march began at J P roundabout near historic Gandhi Maidan , just before noon. Later, police and protesters scuffled at the Dak Bungalow roundabout after AISA-RYA activists were stopped from heading toward Bihar's Lok Bhawan.
In further updates, A large number of student agitators jumped over the barricades near JP Golamber and marched towards the Dak Bungalow.

On top of that, CPI ML MLA from Paliganj, Sandeep Saurav, who was present at the start of the march from gate number 10 of Gandhi Maidan, told reporters that a crisis has struck the country's democracy.

"This is not just an allegation by the opposition, but there have also been several revelations. Despite the differences between the CEC and the two election commissioners, the entire SIR process was carried out. We want the resignation of the CEC," Saurav shared.

title: Pinarayi Vijayan accuses UDF govt of using police to suppress democratic protests in Keralam
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Adding to this, Pinarayi Vijayan accuses UDF govt of using police to suppress democratic protests in Keralam In a Facebook post, Vijayan referred to the alleged police brutality against protesting Students Federation of India activists in Palakkad of late and the lathi charge against members of the CPI's student wing at a Kerala University hostel last month. Meanwhile, The Marxist veteran claimed the incidents showed the Home Department had failed in its duties.
Notably, He warned that if the government did not immediately rein in the police and ensure that the force acted in accordance with the law, the state would witness strong public protests.
As per the latest buzz, The former CM claimed that SFI activists, including female students, were brutally assaulted in Palakkad of late by a police officer who was allegedly drunk.

title: Drishyam 3 worldwide box office collection: Ajay Devgn film nears ₹500 crore, collects ₹490 crore despite drop
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window earnings: Ajay Devgn -starrer Drishyam 3: The Conclusion began its box-office journey on a strong note. After two money-spinning weeks, the movie witnessed a steep drop of almost 72% on its second Monday. However, despite the decline, the thriller continued to hold its ground, with its worldwide collection inching closer to the coveted ₹ 500-crore rupees mark.

Adding to this, Ajay Devgn's movie Drishyam 3 is set to cross ₹500 crore rupees mark. (HT_PRINT) Drishyam 3 worldwide collection The Ajay Devgn movie collected ₹ 245.50 crore rupees during the first week of its rollout. On its second Friday, it collected around ₹ 14 crore rupees before witnessing a significant jump over the weekend, earning ₹ 26.50 crore rupees on Saturday and ₹ 22.50 crore rupees on Sunday. Drishyam 3: The Conclusion saw a sharp decline on Monday, collecting a net of ₹ 6.25 crore rupees across 13,605 shows.

Meanwhile, This took the movie’s total India net collection to ₹ 315.25 crore rupees, while its India gross collection reached ₹ 378.24 crore rupees. The movie collected ₹ 2.50 crore rupees overseas on Monday, taking its total overseas gross to ₹ 111.50 crore rupees. This pushed its worldwide gross collection to ₹ 489.74 crore rupees.

Notably, Comparisons between the Ajay Devgn-starrer and the Malayalam version of Drishyam, led by Mohanlal, have been a talking point since the Hindi movie’s rollout. Many Malayalam followers have lauded the Ajay Devgn-starrer, some even calling it better than the Mohanlal's movie. Of late, Mohanlal shared a video praising Ajay’s movie. Ajay reposted the video and thanked the veteran star for his review.

As per the latest buzz, Sharing the video, Mohanlal shared, “I watched Drishyam The Conclusion and I am truly impressed with the way they have brought much loved journey to a befitting end. Congratulations to Abhishek Pathak, Kumar Mangat Pathak, Ajay Devgn and the entire cast and crew on a job so well done.”
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Star Studio18 (@starstudio18)

On top of that, Drishyam 3 has also become the biggest movie of Ajay Devgn’s career. After recording the biggest opening of his career, the movie has minted ₹ 489.74 crore rupees worldwide, surpassing his previous biggest hits, Singham Again (approximately ₹ 372.5 crore rupees) and Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior (approximately ₹ 368.75 crore rupees), to become his highest-grossing movie ever.

Directed by Abhishek Pathak, Drishyam 3: The Conclusion is the third and final instalment in the Hindi Drishyam franchise. title: Celina Jaitly says she ‘begged’ Austrian husband Peter Haag for amicable separation; Lara Dutta is ‘witness’ to her dedication to family
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Celina Jaitly has been vocal on social media about her issues with her estranged husband, Austrian businessman Peter Haag. Since the couple separated, she has detailed her ordeal, alleging domestic violence against her husband in their divorce case. In her most recent post, the star shared pictures of her children and wrote that she ‘begged’ for an amicable separation from her husband but was denied it. She also called Lara Dutta and Dimpy Ganguli, among others, as witnesses to her dedication to her family.

Adding to this, Star Celina Jaitly married Austrian businessman Peter Haag in 2010. Celina Jaitly says she ‘begged’ Peter Haag for amicable separation Celina looked back on the year that had passed since she had arrived in Mumbai after separating from Peter. “1 year ago, on 12th Oct, I arrived in Mumbai with a ticket booked on a credit card & 1 suitcase: files, my late ma’s saree & heartbreak. Most difficult decision of my life! In early Sept 2025, I was driven to the post office for what I believed was our 15th wedding anniversary gift. It was a divorce notice.”

Meanwhile, She shared that when she asked for an amicable separation, she was asked to work as a cleaner to afford legal fees. “At our first hearing..The judge gave us until Nov to work towards an amicable separation. I begged my husband: “I promise I will not tell the court about ur abuse & trauma. Let us separate amicably for the children… For my brother… how will I pay for litigation?” “Speak to my lawyers.” I was told to work as a cleaner if I ran short of legal fees. 15 years of marriage & 4 children. Was this the same man?” wrote Celina.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Celina Vikram Jaitly (@celinajaitlyofficial)

As per the latest buzz, Celina also claims that she was told she couldn’t leave Austria if she wanted access to their children. “Next day, a legal notice claimed all my premarital assets. I was told I could not leave Austria after divorce if I wanted access to my children. I had no access to our Austrian accounts & discovered efforts to sell my premarital assets in India,” she detailed, adding, “My brother’s situation weighed heavily too. Under constant surveillance, my scolding the children for silly things started being recorded to portray me as mentally unsound, incapable mother. How could I bring my children into uncertainty in India, barred from my own home?”

In further updates, “With my Austrian neighbours’ help, I left at 1 a.m. I spent a week in a hotel, in conversation with my children on Zoom & phone calls. The day I went to court to reclaim my premarital assets, all contact was severed. One twin messaged that their father was screaming that I had abandoned them. A year later, efforts continue to take away my joint custody . My children being brainwashed alienated & moved continuously through Austrian jurisdictions,” she claimed about her children.

On top of that, Celina reinstated her love for her children, claiming, “My witnesses include former UN chief global issues, Lara Dutta, a constant visitor in UAE our children a month apart; my Dubai neighbours TV star Dimpy Ganguly; the German head of the parent-teacher group GISS, Canadian Pakistani pediatrician; my British gynaecologist & neighbour; Austrian doctors & all my village neighbours. They stand witness for my motherhood & dedication to my family & children.”

She ended her note with, “Yet I await justice. This is the story of a mother who continues to fight…” The picture Celina posted shows her with her older twins, Winston and Viraaj, who were born in 2012, and her younger son, Arthur, born in 2017. Arthur’s twin, Shamsher, died after birth due to a heart condition. Celina and Peter married in Hyderabad in 2010. The star filed for divorce in a Mumbai court in November 2025.

title: Mrunal Thakur says ‘haven’t signed a film in 9 months' amid rumours of being a part of Atlee, Allu Arjun and Deepika Padukone's Raaka
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

One of the most anticipated sci-fi films is Atlee’s Raaka. The movie brings together Telugu star Allu Arjun and Bollywood star Deepika Padukone , making for an exciting on-screen pairing. There have also been reports that Mrunal Thakur is joining the cast of Raaka. However, in a recent interview with Mid-Day, the star reacted to the rumours.

Adding to this, Mrunal Thakur neither denies nor confirms being a part of Atlee and Allu Arjun's Raaka. Mrunal Thakur on being a part of Raaka When asked about being part of Raaka, Mrunal neither verified nor denied the reports but added, "I haven't signed any movie in almost nine months. I'm waiting for a meaningful role to come [my way]. Now, whatever announcement has to happen, it will happen on my social media handle and then I'd love to talk about it."

Meanwhile, She further explained why she had not signed any films, clarifying that it was not because she was short of offers. She added, "But I don't resonate with the stories that are being made. So, I have chosen to take some time off because I don't want to question why I'm on set every day. I have to spend 120 days on a movie set. title: Judge unwell, Supreme Court defers hearing on Delhi protest crackdown till Thursday
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Tuesday adjourned to October 15 a clutch of petitions challenging alleged detentions, assault of protesters and sweeping restrictions on public transport ahead of a demonstration demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, as one of the judges on the bench was unwell.

Adding to this, On Saturday, hundreds of protesters who were not allowed to gather at Jantar Mantar took shelter at Bangla Sahib gurdwara. (HT photo) A bench, comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, deferred the batch of around a dozen petitions after both sides agreed to an adjournment to enable Justice Mohana to recover. The court also granted Delhi Police and other authorities time until Wednesday evening to file their responses to notices issued in contempt proceedings alleging disobedience of its earlier directions.

Meanwhile, The bench shared fresh petitions could also be taken up on Thursday, provided their filing defects were cured. It remains unclear whether a separate petition filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 10 other INDIA bloc leaders, challenging alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission of India (ECI), would be heard alongside the batch.

Notably, The adjournment comes amid mounting legal scrutiny of the police action against protesters in Delhi and restrictions imposed ahead of Saturday’s demonstration called by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and other political groups over alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

As per the latest buzz, On Sunday, a special bench of justices Bagchi and Mohana directed that peaceful, unarmed protesters could not be detained except in accordance with the “procedure established by law”. It also ordered that metro and railway services operate normally, internet connectivity remain undisturbed and free movement be restored, subject to lawful restrictions. The bench further directed authorities to remove notices imposing prohibitory restrictions around the Supreme Court and other court complexes to prevent any apprehension about access to justice.

In further updates, The directions followed allegations that sweeping restrictions had been imposed on public movement, protesters had been detained beyond areas covered by prohibitory orders and the city had witnessed a curfew-like situation. Petitioners also alleged that authorities had failed to comply with an earlier order directing them to reconsider proposed restrictions on metro and railway services rather than shutting them down outright.

On top of that, Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, disputed the allegations, maintaining that metro services had operated normally, although entry and exit were restricted at 45 of the Delhi-NCR network’s 303 stations. The bench sought details of the affected stations and directed the authorities to file affidavits explaining the circumstances in which protesters were detained, the manner of their detention and the legal justification for the action.

The court’s intervention came against the backdrop of concerns raised by lawyers over alleged police excesses, including the detention and manhandling of senior advocates. During Sunday’s hearing, senior advocate Shadan Farasat, appearing for the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (SCAORA), described the situation in Delhi as suppressive, while senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan alleged that lawyers, students, women and children had been pushed, shoved or assaulted during the crackdown.

title: Anti-SIR protests: Karnataka home minister Kharge orders review of police action
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge on Tuesday ordered a review of the detention of protesters ahead of a march in Bengaluru against the electoral roll Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and to press for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the process, saying peaceful demonstrations must be protected. He shared that dissent must not be treated as a threat to law and order.

Adding to this, Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge. (X) The protesters, including students, senior citizens, activists and lawyers, were detained on Monday before they could march to the Chief Electoral Officer’s office in Bengaluru. Organisers alleged police seized placards, dragged demonstrators into buses and assaulted protesters, including women and journalists.

Meanwhile, Kharge shared the handling of the protesters will be reviewed. “The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. It must be respected, protected and never suppressed,” Kharge shared in a note on Tuesday. He shared he had instructed the police to ensure peaceful demonstrations are not disrupted. He appealed to protesters to cooperate with the police while keeping authorities informed of their plans. “Our responsibility is not merely to maintain law and order, but to create an environment where every citizen can express dissent freely, peacefully and without fear.”

Notably, The march was organised under the banner of the My Vote, My Right Campaign, a coalition of over 40 civil society organisations, opposed to the SIR. The organisers planned to submit a memorandum to Karnataka chief electoral officer V Anbukkumar seeking cancellation of the SIR, restoration of electoral rolls as they were in January 2025 and Kumar’s resignation.

As per the latest buzz, They alleged that the Bengaluru police detained some participants before the march had begun. Some were allegedly pushed and dragged into buses. The organisers shared young people were beaten and women’s clothing was pulled.
In further updates, In a statement, the organisers shared four police personnel beat a photojournalist, while three other journalists were manhandled.

title: 4 FIRs filed after INDIA bloc's march to Supreme Court amid anti-EC protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police have registered four First Information Reports (FIRs) in connection with the INDIA bloc’s protest march against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar on Monday, on grounds of alleged violation of prohibitory orders in and around Connaught Place and the Supreme Court, a police officer shared.

Adding to this, Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Imran Pratapgarhi and Deepender Singh Hooda, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, and others INDIA bloc leaders proceed in a bus towards the Supreme Court in Delhi on Monday. (PTI) Two FIRs have been registered at Tilak Marg police station, while Mandir Marg and Barakhamba Road police stations have registered one FIR each, the officer shared on condition of anonymity. The prohibitory orders were imposed under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

Meanwhile, The development came a day after thousands of protesters, including opposition parties, gathered in central Delhi, in one of the largest political mobilisations in the Capital in recent years. Monday’s demonstration came following two days of police action against protesters.

Notably, On Monday, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi led the march from Constitution Club towards the Supreme Court, where he sought an independent, time-bound investigation into decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by Kumar and demanded that the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls be suspended pending the inquiry.

As per the latest buzz, The march was initially scheduled to begin at 1.30pm but did not start until around 4pm. However, thousands of people, including activists and other supporters, began gathering at Barakhamba Road and Connaught Place intersection, raising slogans and carrying flags. Police personnel cordoned off the area, erected barricades and diverted traffic as the gathering grew.

In further updates, Opposition leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Tejashwi Yadav and Communist Party of India (Marxist) general secretary MA Baby, met at the Constitution Club to finalise the petition before the march.

On top of that, The petition, which named the Election Commission of India, Kumar and two other election commissioners as respondents, was flagged for 14 defects, including a shortfall of ₹ 220 in court fees, an illegible photocopy of Kharge’s identity card and missing vakalatnamas for nine of the 11 petitioners. The legal team requested that the matter be listed on Thursday.

In a post on X, Gandhi thanked those who participated in the protest and supporters who backed the demonstration remotely at 3pm. “Today was a very important day because we needed to show the government that the people of India are not going to be intimidated,” he wrote.

title: Kiran Bedi backs Jantar Mantar de-notification, explains why site is ‘least suited’ for protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Former IPS officer Kiran Bedi has backed the decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a protest site, saying the location was ill-suited for demonstrations because of its narrow lanes and proximity to sensitive buildings and offices.

Adding to this, Former Puducherry Lieutenant Governor Kiran Bedi (VISHAL KAPOOR) In a post on X, Bedi shared every city needed designated spaces for democratic expression, arguing that the administration had erred in choosing Jantar Mantar and failed to correct the decision earlier. Her remarks come after the Delhi Police, in an order issued on October 11, designated Ramlila Maidan, Burari Maidan and CBD Ground in Shahdara as alternative venues for protests.

Meanwhile, “During my lifetime of policing the city of Delhi, I have seen protest sites shift from the PM’s residence and Teen Murti Marg (then Mrs Gandhi’s residence) to the roads of Lutyens’ Delhi in the early 1970s, then to India Gate in the 1980s, and later to Jantar Mantar,” she wrote.
Notably, “Every city requires an open space for democratic expression, which we also call a protest, but forgets to provide for,” she added.

As per the latest buzz, Bedi urged city planners to take note, arguing that Jantar Mantar was the least suited to serve as a protest site because of its narrow lanes, proximity to sensitive buildings and offices, and location near Connaught Place, a major commercial hub.
In further updates, “I think the administration of that time erred in taking that decision and did not correct it all this while. And the consequences are there to see,” she wrote.
On top of that, She shared the Union home ministry had identified Ramlila Maidan and other locations for protests, adding that the shift perhaps required judicial intervention.
“Now we need a clear security and functioning plan for Ramlila Maidan to be shared when according permissions,” Bedi added.

title: 'Not the official stance': Harvard Club of India clarifies after alumni statement on Delhi protest crackdown
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Harvard Club of India, the official alumni group of the United States' prestigious Harvard University alumni in India, clarified on Monday that it did not endorse or issue any statement regarding the ongoing protests in Delhi.

Adding to this, On October 10, about 41,000 security personnel turned the Capital into a fortress on Saturday to thwart the planned protest. (file/AFP) The club was referring to a letter as per reports issued by 100 Harvard University alumni condemning "police brutality, unlawful detention, and violations of constitutional rights of all peaceful protestors" in Delhi during the protest held on October 10 against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision exercise.

Meanwhile, On Saurday, October 10, about 41,000 security personnel turned the Capital into a fortress on Saturday to thwart the planned protest and launched an unprecedented clampdown that saw the detention of 7,000 people and left large chunks of Delhi deserted.
Notably, However, the club on Monday distanced itself from the reported letter and shared that the statement did not represent the organisation's official position.

As per the latest buzz, Rajat Sethi, a member of the club's Executive Committee, told news agency ANI that some Harvard University alumni had issued the letter without representing the organisation. He shared the clarification was necessary because the club had not issued or endorsed any statement on the protests or the detentions that followed.

In further updates, “As a member of the elected body of the Executive Council of the Harvard Club of India, which is the official alumni group of Harvard University alumni in India, I wanted to issue a clarification that certain individuals have gone ahead and issued a letter remarking on and making comments about the recent protest and the detention that followed. I wanted to issue a clarification that this is not the official position of the Harvard Club of India,” Sethi shared.
On top of that, He added that the club's charter and mandate do not permit it to issue political statements either in its own name or on behalf of Harvard University.

“Therefore, this clarification is to explain to the larger audience that certain individuals who happen to be alumni of Harvard University have issued the statement in their personal capacity. While we respect personal expression, that is not a substitute for institutional representation,” he shared.

title: Who is Neha Bora? AISA president at centre of anti-CEC, SIR protests breaking internet
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

All India Students' Association president Neha Bora has emerged as one of the prominent faces representing student activists – whether it be the paper leak protests earlier this year or the present stir against the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the special intensive revision exercise of electoral rolls.

Adding to this, Neha Bora was among the student leaders who joined education reformer Sonam Wangchuk in an indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar earlier this year. (REUTERS) Bora is a 29-year-old PhD scholar at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) and the national president of AISA. They have been among the activists detained several times by the Delhi Police over the last week, amid the agitation against the CEC. Bora also led separate protests in the Capital over the issue, with senior advocates Prashant Bhushan and Kapil Sibal also joining them in the protest march last week.

Meanwhile, Bora, a research scholar at JNU’s School of Arts and Aesthetics, had always been involved in student politics on campus. Originally from Uttarakhand, they completed their undergraduate studies at Delhi University before pursuing a master’s degree at Ambedkar University Delhi, as per the latest buzz.

Notably, According to Bora, their political views have differed sharply from their family. In an interview with Frontline, Bora shared, “My family is staunch BJP supporters, and we have had very big disagreements in my house."

As per the latest buzz, Bora was among the student leaders who joined education reformer Sonam Wangchuk in an indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar as part of the wider student-led protests spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over alleged examination irregularities.

In further updates, The stir eventually led to the resignation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Bora had also participated in the protests in Jharkhand over alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission examinations.. During the stir, an unidentified man allegedly threw ink at them, but Bora continued their agitation, saying the incident would not intimidate them.

On top of that, While several Cockroach Janta Party leaders and other activists were detained ahead of the October 10 agitation in Delhi, Bora gave a protest call with an alternative location as Jantar Mantar remained out of reach. “Dilli Haat becomes Jantar Mantar today! See you there!” Bora wrote in a post on X. Bora and other activists were later detained by the Delhi Police during the protest.

Bora spoke against the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site. “Taking away Jantar Mantar will not take way the resistance. All your attempts to 'denotify' democracy by denotifying Jantar Mantar will fail. The people will prevail!” they shared in a post on X.

title: Shekhar Suman recalls last moments of 11-year-old son, says wife begged doctors to let him go: ‘Couldn’t bear to see him suffer’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Shekhar Suman of late opened up about the most difficult phase of his life, when he lost his 11-year-old son, Aayush. The child suffered from a rare, incurable heart condition called endomyocardial fibrosis (EMF) and passed away due to the illness in 1995.

Adding to this, Shekhar Suman spoke about the death of his 11-year-old son. 'Papa, I don’t want to go. Please save me' In conversation with The Lallantop, Shekhar recalled how he was struggling to find work when he learnt about his son's diagnosis. With Aayush terminally ill, he eventually decided to take up television projects to support his family. He chose to work on the TV show Dekh Bhai Dekh, produced by Jaya Bachchan, and recalled keeping his phone close to him during shoots so he could stay updated about his son's health.

Meanwhile, Shekhar also recalled the final moments of his son’s life. He shared, “Before his death, he had started reciting Sanskrit shlokas. He was 11. I don’t know how he did it. He shared he saw a golden light coming, held my hand and told me, ‘Papa, I don’t want to go. Please save me.’ Then he started reciting some Sanskrit shlokas, and we were flustered. He then told each one of us who were with him at that time, including our driver, that he loved us. He was like an angel; he was a beautiful child. I still don’t know how that tragedy happened to us. But I guess that’s destiny. There’s no bigger tragedy that can befall parents than losing their children."

Notably, Shekhar recalled that his son’s condition deteriorated to such an extent that his wife, Alka Suman, eventually pleaded with doctors to let him go. “His condition worsened so much that at one point, my wife begged the doctors to let him go. I told her, ‘What are you saying? We will fight till the end.’ But she shared, ‘This is the end. Let him go; he is suffering a lot.’ She was the ‘savvy mother who begged for her son’s death.’ She was right, we couldn’t bear seeing him suffer like that,” he added.
As per the latest buzz, Shekhar admitted that after his son’s death, he lost interest in money and fame. However, he continued working to support the rest of his family.
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shekhar Tonite (@shekhartonite)

On top of that, Shekhar Suman hosted a digital talk show called Shekhar Tonite, which premiered on May 15, 2026,and of late concluded its first eason. The show marked his highly anticipated return to the late-night talk show format and political satire after nearly 14 years away from the genre, following his run with Movers & Shakers.

Defending the industry, she shared actors are generally respectful towards women who balance motherhood and their careers.

Meanwhile, She shared, "See, I don't think women should listen to anybody commenting on their body. Industry is very respectful of women who have babies and who have careers. All the fantastic actresses from Madhuri to Juhi Chawla to Rani Mukherjee, Sonali Bendre. I don't think it's the industry. It's the common man of India who is ugly and balding and has a disgusting paunch who thinks that commenting on Katrina Kaif or Aishwarya Rai is somehow making his life better. It's so funny. I find it really useless and I honestly do think that it deserves much less space even in media discourse."
Notably, Richa further defended the movie industry, saying that the anonymity offered by social media emboldens people to target celebrities who have achieved far more than they have.

As per the latest buzz, She shared, "Industry is not like this. It's common people who have been emboldened by the anonymity of social media. Who think that they have hit the jackpot by leaving anonymous comments. They are beggars in their lives. But they think that they can talk about people who are like Miss World and Miss Universe. Like we owe them something. That's not how the world works. They are just losers and they deserve to be ignored."
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Katrina Kaif (@katrinakaif)
On top of that, At a recent event in the UK, Katrina addressed online trolling and explained why she does not let it affect her self-worth.

She shared, “I think we really need to be careful in letting the narrative on social media affect our self-worth. If we start trying to cater to all of them, I think that really hampers your ability to make choices for yourself. Personally, if every time I face critique or comments, I let that dictate my actions, I think I would have been paralysed with fear and unable to move ahead in my life.”

title: Opposition takes CEC protest to Supreme Court
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Opposition on Monday led thousands of people who flooded central Delhi for three hours in protest against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, marking one of the largest political mobilisations in recent years that followed two days of police crackdown on agitators.

Adding to this, All INDIA bloc members marched from Barakhamba Road to Supreme Court. (PTI) Congress leader Rahul Gandhi led the march from the Constitution Club to Bhagwan Das Road and later walked into the Supreme Court to file a petition demanding an independent, time-bound investigation into decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by Kumar and to suspend the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) pending this inquiry.

Meanwhile, The petition – which named the Election Commission of India, Kumar and two other election commissioners as respondents – was flagged for 14 defects, including a ₹ 220 shortfall in court fees, an illegible photocopy of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s identity card and missing vakalatnamas for nine of the 11 petitioners. The petitioners’ legal team requested that the matter be listed on Thursday.

Notably, “I’d like to thank every single person who came out today for this protest. I’d also like to thank the millions of people who showed support in their own way at 3pm. Thank you to the leaders of INDIA bloc, all the workers of the Congress party and workers of the INDIA bloc,” Gandhi posted on X.
As per the latest buzz, “Today was a very important day because we needed to show the government that the people of India are not going to be intimidated,” he added.

In further updates, All Opposition leaders including Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, Rashtriya Janata Dal chief Tejaswi Yadav and Communist Party of India (Marxist) general secretary MA Baby met at Constitution Club to finalise the petition. The march from Barakhamba Road to Supreme Court, scheduled at 1.30pm, could not start before 4pm.

On top of that, But thousands of people – commoners and activists alike – started gathering at the Barakhamba Road and Connaught Place intersection in anticipation, shouting slogans and hoisting flags. Several police and security personnel cordoned off the march, erected barricades and diverted traffic.

Two student leaders– Neha Bora of the All India Student Association and former Jawaharlal Nehru University students union president N Sai Balaji – shared the stage with the Opposition brass. A senior Opposition leader shared it was to acknowledge the student stirs.

Adding to this, India News Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan shared the Congress is “rudderless and directionless” and therefore, has chosen to deflect attention from its own electoral failures by pinning the blame on the poll panel.

title: Jantar Mantar’s changing place in Delhi’s protest map
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police on Monday de-notified Jantar Mantar in Lutyen’s Delhi as a designated protest venue, naming Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in Shahdara , venues spread out across the city, as the new sites for demonstrations.

Adding to this, In this file photo friends and relatives of Aarushi Talwar light candles near her portrait to seek justice for her at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi in Jan 2011. (HT File Photo) The move comes two days after the Supreme Court called for authorities to consider better-equipped alternatives, but it revives a constitutional question the court confronted in 2018: how can the State regulate protests without effectively shutting down a space for dissent?

Meanwhile, Jantar Mantar was built as an astronomical observatory, but its adjoining road gradually acquired another role. It became a place where citizens could make their grievances visible to the political establishment. After demonstrations at the Boat Club lawns near India Gate were restricted following a major farmers’ agitation in the 1980s, Jantar Mantar became, from around 1993, the principal venue where protests in the capital were permitted.

Notably, Protesters could gather within sight of Parliament and government offices, but the compact stretch of road also made demonstrations easier to contain than large marches through the city. The 2018 Supreme Court judgment recorded arguments that the site offered protesters greater visibility and that shifting them farther away risked diluting their message.

As per the latest buzz, The venue hosted demonstrations by farmers, trade unions, political parties, students, civil society groups and individuals pursuing personal causes. Some gatherings were brief; others became prolonged occupations, with tents and temporary structures remaining in place. That persistence, and the accompanying use of loudspeakers and public-address systems, soon became a source of conflict with residents.

In further updates, In October 2017, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) accepted a complaint by residents of Jantar Mantar Road, noting that demonstrations had become continuous and were causing noise and air pollution, sanitation problems and disruption to their daily lives. Residents also complained that protesters had put up tents and other structures and that some had remained for months or years.

On top of that, The NGT’s October 2017 order directed the Delhi government, New Delhi Municipal Council and Delhi police commissioner to stop dharnas, protests, public speeches and loudspeaker use on Jantar Mantar Road. It also ordered the removal of temporary structures and waste, and directed that protesters be shifted to Ramlila Maidan.

The order brought the site’s role as a protest venue to an abrupt halt. It framed the dispute primarily as one of environmental harm and residents’ rights, but the protesters and supporting organisations argued that a complete prohibition also cut off a practical, visible platform for peaceful assembly proximate to the seat of government.

title: Jantar Mantar no longer Delhi’s protest site as police designate 3 new venues amid anti-CEC stir in capital
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

For 33 years, an 18th-century astronomical observatory in the heart of Delhi functioned as a lighthouse for causes big and small – former soldiers demanding parity in pensions, a woman on hunger strike spotlighting army excesses, sexual violence victims hoping for justice, queer people dreaming of dignity, and a generation imagining a future free of corruption.

Adding to this, Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground have been designated as alternative locations for demonstrations in the Capital. (AFP) In the aftermath of the sprawling NEET agitation this summer that forced the education minister’s resignation and the ongoing stir against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar , police have denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, ending its standing as the country’s most iconic site for dissent, all within a stone’s throw of the corridors of power in Lutyens Delhi.

Meanwhile, The order – signed by police commissioner Anurag Kumar and dated October 11 – also designated three new protest venues: Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground in north Delhi and CBD Ground in east Delhi. The first is spread across 12 acres and hosts thousands all year round. The other two are on the fringes of Delhi – 18km and 12.4km away from Jantar Mantar , respectively.

Notably, The order, titled “Guidelines for Holding Protests or Demonstrations in Delhi”, shared the Union ministry of home affairs constituted a committee to “examine alternative proper venues for citizen’s right for organising protest/demonstrations in place of the existing ‘designated site’”.

As per the latest buzz, “Based on the committee’s recommendations, Jantar Mantar as a protest venue has been de-notified,” the order shared, adding that three new venues were designated for organising protests and demonstrations.

In further updates, While Ramlila Maidan is the closest to central Delhi, it is a paid venue that is already in demand for seasonal events. CBD Ground is surrounded by residential and commercial developments, while Burari Ground lies on the outskirts of the Capital.

On top of that, The controversial decision came days after the Supreme Court urged authorities to identify a spacious and open alternative protest site equipped with basic amenities instead of Jantar Mantar. On October 9, the top court shared Delhi should consider a larger spot with toilets, drinking water, medical assistance and space for emergency access. The bench shared the city should identify a venue that would allow peaceful demonstrations while protecting public safety and access to essential services.

In October 2017, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) directed the Delhi government, New Delhi Municipal Council and Delhi police commissioner to stop dharnas, protests, public speeches and the use of loudspeakers on Jantar Mantar Road. It also ordered the removal of temporary structures and waste, and directed that protesters be shifted to Ramlila Maidan.

title: After week-long anti-EC protests, a brief pause in Delhi
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

After a week of high-octane protests that included five major marches in different parts of the city, the Congress leadership might take some time to launch the next round of demonstrations for the ouster of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Adding to this, Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar, Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Imran Pratapgarhi and Deepender Hooda, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, and others INDIA bloc leaders proceed in a bus towards the Supreme Court to file a petition against Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged poll irregularities during 'March for Democracy', in New Delhi, Monday. (PTI) The party leadership has informed the INDIA allies that another march or demonstration is unlikely to take place on Tuesday. But the Congress’s frontal organisations, especially the Indian Youth Congress (IYC) or the student body National Students Union of India (NSUI), might carry on their own protests.

Meanwhile, On October 6, the Congress-led INDIA bloc began its intensive protests with a march from Parliament to the Election Commission, but the march was stopped midway near Akashvani Bhavan—less than 300 meters from the poll body’s headquarters.

Notably, The next day, the lawmakers tried to march from Janpath to Jantar Mantar, but the Delhi police stopped them at the busy intersection of Raisina Road and Ashoka Road, and the leaders were detained. The INDIA bloc led a march to the Rajghat on last Thursday, followed by a march from Parliament to the Rashtrapati Bhavan to submit a memorandum to President Droupadi Murmu.

As per the latest buzz, The Opposition on Monday took out arguably the biggest political march in recent times to the Supreme Court complex and filed a fresh petition against the vote chori (vote theft), as the protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar intensified and spilled over to the second week, with the leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, announcing that the demonstration will continue to save the Constitution.
In further updates, On Monday evening, the Congress leaders called their allies to inform them that no such demonstrations had been proposed for Tuesday.

On top of that, “I got a call from Congress. They believe that after the successful march to the Supreme Court and filing of a petition, there is no need for another march or demonstrations on Tuesday,” CPIM general secretary MA Baby told HT.

Trinamool Congress’s (Mamata faction) Rajya Sabha floor leader Derek O’Brien shared that with the festive season round the corner, starting with the Durga Puja, the Opposition parties might have to chalk out their own plans.

title: Nushrratt Bharuccha finds comfort in Shah Rukh Khan-Kajol’s Gerua in hospital, recovering from spine surgery after Bali accident: ‘Healing slowly’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nushrratt Bharuccha found a reason to smile in the middle of a difficult recovery, thanks to Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol. The star, who of late underwent spine surgery after an accident in Bali , shared a video from her hospital room on Monday, showing the Bollywood magic that is keeping her spirits up.

Adding to this, Nushrratt Bharuccha turns to SRK and Kajol’s Gerua during spine surgery recovery: ‘Healing slowly, dreaming endlessly’. Nushrrat Bharuccha shares health update In the video posted on her Instagram Stories on Monday, Nushrratt is seen smiling from her hospital bed as Gerua, the romantic song featuring Shah Rukh and Kajol in Dilwale, plays on the television. Medical staff are also seen helping her with her meal. Sharing the moment, the star spoke about finding happiness in small things while getting better.

Meanwhile, "And just like that, Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol bring a smile to my face. A reminder, things get better ... little by little... they always do. Healing slowly, dreaming endlessly," she captioned the post.

Notably, A few days before sharing the video, Nushrratt had posted a photograph of an empty reclining wheelchair near a window, with the sunset in the background. It was her first social media update since the accident, and her caption hinted at how much life had changed in a short time. She wrote, “Been chasing sunsets forever, and just like that my view changed. But, Picture abhi baaki hai mere dost.”

As per the latest buzz, Nushrratt suffered a spinal fracture during what her team described as a “work-cum-holiday trip” to Bali. She was first taken to a hospital in Indonesia and later flown back to Mumbai in an air ambulance for surgery.

In further updates, Her publicist verified the news in a statement, saying, “Nushrratt Bharuccha, who was in Bali for a work-cum-holiday trip, met with an unfortunate accident and suffered a fracture in her spine.”

On top of that, The statement also shared that her “immediate priority is her health and ensuring she receives the necessary medical care.” It added that she would need “time to rest and recover,” with her professional commitments likely to be affected over the following weeks. Videos showing Nushrratt arriving in Mumbai on a stretcher also circulated online, leaving followers worried about her condition.
The accident comes at a time when Nushrratt has projects lined up. She was last seen in the Netflix movie Ufff Yeh Siyapaa, alongside Sohum Shah and Nora Fatehi.

title: 'No eligible voter to be left out': States hold special voter enrolment camps amid anti-SIR, CEC protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Chief electoral officers (CEOs) of several states and Union territories have shared no eligible voter will be left out of the electoral rolls, announcing special enrolment camps at polling stations, schools and colleges as part of a drive ordered by the Election Commission of India (ECI).

Adding to this, The drive follows ECI instructions issued on October 1 to enrol eligible electors who were left out. (Ishant Chauhan/HT) Revealed via CEOs’ official social media handles on Monday, this comes amid nationwide protests over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Meanwhile, In Rajasthan, 41 district election officers (DEOs) have started a “proactive campaign”, with camps being held at 61,404 booths, the state CEO shared. Chhattisgarh’s 33 DEOs have launched a similar drive across 27,196 booths, and camps are also being held in schools and colleges. Kerala shared camps are being held at village offices for all 30,471 booths across its 14 districts.
Notably, Similar announcements were made by CEOs of other states and UTs including Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, and Haryana.

As per the latest buzz, In Odisha, camps are being organised at 45,250 polling booths across the state. In Ladakh, electors are being facilitated through 595 polling stations. The Lakshadweep administration shared special camps are being held across the Union territory. In Jharkhand, officials inspected special camps at polling stations in Bhojudih, among other places.

In further updates, The drive follows ECI instructions issued on October 1 to enrol eligible electors who were left out. In Chhattisgarh, the campaign began on October 8, with BLOs visiting homes, schools and colleges, and holding camps at booths.

On top of that, Voters with complaints have been asked to contact booth-level officers (BLOs), assistant electoral registration officers (AEROs), electoral registration officers (EROs) or DEOs. Rajasthan has listed 61,404 BLOs, 854 AEROs, 200 EROs and 41 DEOs for this. Kerala has 30,471 BLOs and 140 each of AEROs and AEROs. Lakshadweep has 64 BLOs, 10 AEROs, one ERO and one DEO.

Delhi’s CEO shared about 3.3 million entries in the capital’s voter list had been flagged under “logical discrepancy” or as un-mapped, and around 2 million of them have been resolved. It listed 14,947 BLOs, 902 AEROs, 70 EROs and 13 DEOs for grievances.

title: Ramesh Taurani recalls Alka Yagnik’s rise in the ’90s: “She was getting the most songs”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Discussing the music landscape of the period, Ramesh Taurani recalled that established voices such as Lata Mangeshkar and Asha Bhosle continued to be important choices for filmmakers, while a new generation of singers was gaining prominence.
Adding to this, “Back then, Lata Ji and Asha Ji were already established. When we used to make music, Lata Ji was our first preference, followed by Alka and Anuradha,” Taurani shared.

Meanwhile, He went on to recall the emergence of singers including Kumar Sanu, Anuradha Paudwal, Alka Yagnik and Udit Narayan. According to him, films such as Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak , Aashiqui , Saajan and Phool Aur Kaante helped establish the new voices in the industry as their songs became popular with audiences.

Notably, “The idea was that in the ’90s, when new singers like Shanu, Anuradha Paudwal, Alka Yagnik and Udit Narayan came in, these four made it big. Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak , Aashiqui , Saajan and Phool Aur Kaante were hits, and their songs became superhits,” he recalled.

As per the latest buzz, Taurani also drew a comparison between the newer singers and the established female playback voices of the previous generation. He recalled that Anuradha Paudwal was being viewed as a successor to Lata Mangeshkar, while Alka Yagnik was increasingly being positioned as a voice comparable to Asha Bhosle.

body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 11: Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam: The Conclusion is showing no signs of slowing down at the ticket-window. The movie crossed the ₹ 300 crore rupees mark on its tenth day. It has also emerged as the biggest ticket-window success of Ajay's career, giving the star a new career high.

Adding to this, According to trade tracker Sacnilk, the crime thriller has collected over ₹ 313 crore rupees net in India in just 11 days, following another strong weekend in theatres. The movie coll ected ₹ 4.98 crore rupees net in India on Day 11, taking its total domestic collection to ₹ 313.98 crore rupees, according to live ticket-window tracking data. The movie recorded these numbers across 13,594 shows on Monday.

Meanwhile, The second weekend gave the movie another boost. After earning ₹ 14.50 crore rupees on its second Friday, Day 8, collections rose to ₹ 26.50 crore rupees on Saturday, Day 9, across 14,903 shows. The movie added another ₹ 22.50 crore rupees on Sunday, Day 10, from 14,872 shows. Although Sunday's collection was 15.1% lower than Saturday's, the movie still enjoyed a strong weekend and crossed the ₹ 300 crore rupees mark within ten days of rollout.

Notably, The movie's ticket-window run has taken Ajay Devgn past his previous career record. Drishyam 3 has overtaken Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior to become his highest-grossing movie so far. It is also the first Ajay-led movie to cross ₹ 300 crore rupees in India net collections.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Abhishek Pathak, Drishyam 3: The Conclusion features Ajay Devgn, Tabu, Jaideep Ahlawat, Shriya Saran and Prakash Raj. Rolled out in theatres on October 2, 2026, the movie brings the popular crime thriller franchise to its concluding chapter. title: 'Mini-India', a space for all: Jantar Mantar's special place on Delhi's protest map
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Till the early 1990s, Jantar Mantar, an 18th century astronomical observatory built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur, was a part of the list of places to sightsee in Delhi , and school students were taken there for annual excursions. In fact, the Misra Yantra inside the Jantar Mantar observatory complex was the inspiration behind the logo of the Asian Games held in New Delhi in 1982.

Adding to this, But Jantar Mantar was not always associated with protesters and posters or barricades and banners. In fact, Boat Club lawns were the preferred protest site, and in 1988, farmer leader Mahendra Singh Tikait led the most significant protest there that lasted a week and saw lakhs of people. Five years later, protests and rallies were banned at Boat Club and the road abutting Jantar Mantar was notified as a designated protest site.

Meanwhile, Called “Mini India” by historian Ramchandra Guha , neem-lined Jantar Mantar is the site that people from across the country gather hoping to be heard. Guha in 'India After Gandhi' describes the transition in 1990s. He notes that Rajpath , where the grounds meant to be empty except on ceremonial days, had become a village of tents, each with colourful placards hung outside it. The people within these tents and the causes they upheld were ever changing. The hill peasants replaced by industrial workers; the Maharashtra farmers by Tibetan refugees; the Konkani speakers by Hindu monks demanding a ban on cow slaughter.

Notably, "In the early nineties, these tents were summarily dismantled by a government worried about the impression made on foreign visitors by such open expression of dissent. Rajpath was vacated of encroachments and the lawns restored to their former glory but the protesters regrouped, and relocated. They now placed themselves a mile to the north-west, next to the Jantar Mantar observatory in Connaught Place. Here they were away from the eyes of the state, but directly in view of the citizens who daily passed through this busy shopping district," Guha writes.

As per the latest buzz, For 33 years, the half a kilometer stretch near the observatory has provided space for all, measuring public discontent, bringing together farmers, workers, veterans, students, activists and citizens protesting against decisions they believed had left them unheard. On an average, the Parliament Street police station receives more than 24,000 requests for permission to hold protests every year. One could walk on this half a kilometer stretch on single street to get a glimpse of grievances across India.

In further updates, In 2017, Tamil Nadu farmers with mice in their hands or their mouths who wanted to draw attention of the government to the agrarian crisis reached Jantar Mantar. In same year, a man from Madhya Pradesh had spent years protesting against government documents declaring him dead and lived in Jantar Mantar. Eleven ex-servicemen recorded the over 700 days of their relay hunger strike for one-rank-one-pension to followers of Asaram Bapu and Rampal who had spent years camping on Mantar, trying to persuade the authorities to free their jailed gurus.

On top of that, The initial protests of the Anna Hazare movement started from Jantar Mantar in April 2011. Not to forget the annual Delhi Queer Pride parade. In 2105, retired Indian military and paramilitary personnel sat there and demanded fair implementation of One Rank One Pension (OROP), with subsequent demonstrations and re-gatherings taking place in 2016, 2019. Parents, relatives and friends of murdered Noida teen Arushi Talwar demanded justice at Jantar Mantar in 2011 and 2013. Even followers of jailed self-styled godmen; animal lovers against use of cow’s milk; dog haters; members of Akhil Bharatiya Joota Maaro Andolan; and a sole protester from Chandauli who believed satellites hacked into people’s brains in his hometown have found themselves at Jantar Mantar over the years.

On Monday, the Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a designated protest venue. An order issued by the Delhi Commissioner of Police Anurag Kumar states that based on recommendations of committee Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), the Jantar Mantar as a protest venue has been de-notified. Three new venues-- Ramlila ground, Burari ground and CBD ground in East Delhi have been designated as new venues for protests and demonstrations.

title: IIIT Ranchi suicide: Students continue protest; seek director’s resignation
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Students continued their protest for the second consecutive day at the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Ranchi, on Monday following the death by suicide of a first-year student on Saturday night.

Adding to this, The incident came to light on Saturday night when hostel residents alerted the institute administration after finding the student’s room locked from the inside. (X) The students accused the institute administration of negligence and failing to provide emergency medical facilities in the hostel. They demanded the immediate resignation of director Rajiv Srivastava.

Meanwhile, “In an attempt to defuse the tense situation, the institute’s chairperson arrived at the protest site to hold talks with the students. However, a standoff ensued before formal discussions could begin. The examinations, which began on October 8, could not be held on Monday due to the agitation,” IIT registrar Munuren Samson Champia shared.

Notably, The students have demanded accountability for the alleged institutional lapses that they claim delayed emergency medical care for the deceased student. They have also called for the director’s immediate resignation, the implementation of a robust, round-the-clock emergency medical system in the hostel premises, and the permanent deployment of a campus doctor and a dedicated ambulance to ensure a swift response to medical emergencies.
As per the latest buzz, Officer-in-charge of Khelgaon police station Nirbhay Kumar verified the students’ demands but declined to elaborate further.

In further updates, “The students are protesting peacefully, and no law and order problem has arisen so far. The students’ demands and their resolution by the institute’s management are internal matters. The police have no role in the matter,” Kumar shared.
On top of that, He added that a case of unnatural death had been registered and an investigation was underway to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the student’s death.

The incident came to light on Saturday night when hostel residents alerted the institute administration after finding the student’s room locked from the inside. The administration subsequently informed the police.

title: Sunny Deol’s Suryaa first look unveiled but the internet isn’t convinced about Hindi remake of Malayalam movie Joseph: ‘Why watch it in theatres?’
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:

Sunny Deol is back after Batwara 1947 , but this time, there is more to his new look than a rugged beard and an intense stare. The motion poster of Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, rolled out on October 12, has got people talking about the star’s turn in a crime thriller. It has also brought up a question that the makers will have to answer: why should audiences watch a remake when the original is already available?

Adding to this, Sunny Deol in Suryaa's first look whereas Joju George in Joseph. Sunny Deol unveils first look and rollout date The first look of Suryaa was unveiled on October 12 along with the rollout date. Sunny looks markedly different from his usual action-hero avatar in his first look motion poster. With a rugged appearance and an intense gaze, he hints at a man haunted by his past and struggling to confront truths he can no longer ignore. The tagline reads, “Torn between his past and present, he uncovers the truth”. The makers describe the protagonist as a man “drawn into a web of unanswered questions and buried truths,” whose investigation “soon takes him into territory far more complex than he anticipated”.

Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram Interestingly, Suryaa is based on Joseph, the 2018 Malayalam movie starring Joju George as a retired police officer drawn into a murder investigation that forces him to confront his own past. With Joseph director M Padmakumar returning to helm the new version, the star gets a chance to step away from his familiar action-hero image and take on a character driven by grief, secrets and personal turmoil.

Notably, The announcement has not been met with excitement by everyone. On X, several users pointed out that Joseph is already available to watch, questioning whether the Hindi version offers enough reason for audiences to buy a theatre ticket. One user wrote: “For those who are unaware, #Suryaa is a remake of Malayalam movie Joseph. Anyone who wants to watch it, can watch it online & save your money on some original movie.”

As per the latest buzz, Another echoed the sentiment: “For those who are asking, #Suryaa starring #SunnyDeol is a REMAKE of Malayalam movie JOSEPH So my question is why would anyone watch it in Theatres if you can watch it ONLINE?” Many also pointed out that the movie will face immense threat at the ticket-window due to the Diwali rollout of Ramayana: Part 1, in which Sunny Deol is playing the role of Hanuman.

In further updates, Despite the criticism, some viewers are interested in seeing Deol in a crime thriller, particularly one that appears to move away from his usual action-heavy roles. One user offered a succinct summary: “Different look! Crime-thriller genre! A cop investigates a double homicide while the secrets from his own life gets revealed. If executed and promoted well, can be a success for #SunnyDeol.”

On top of that, Drishyam, Vikram Vedha and The Departed have all shown how stories can find audiences in different settings and languages. The real test is whether the adaptation respects what worked in the original while giving viewers a reason to experience it again.

When Joseph arrived in theatres in November 2018, few could have predicted just how far the movie would travel. Directed by M. Padmakumar and written by former police officer Shahi Kabir, the thriller was as per reports made on a budget of ₹ 3 crore rupees and went on to earn ₹ 28 crore rupees. It also completed a run of more than 100 days in theatres.

title: Sonali Bendre tells Madhuri Dixit why she chose to love her body during cancer battle despite immense pain
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sonali Bendre has been open about her battle with cancer and of late spoke about her approach to dealing with the disease. At the grand premiere of Kon Honar Crorepati, the Marathi version of Kaun Banega Crorepati hosted by Madhuri Dixit , the star reflected on how the experience changed her perspective on her body and life.

Adding to this, Sonali Bendre spoke about cancer battle on Kon Honar Crorepati. During the episode, Madhuri lauded Sonali for battling and overcoming cancer. Sonali, however, offered a different perspective, explaining that she had never chosen to look at the experience as a battle. Instead, she focused on understanding her body, treating it with love and learning from one of the most challenging phases of her life.

Meanwhile, Sharing her experience of dealing with cancer, Sonali shared, “I mean, you know, actually, we always say that someone has overcome cancer. But, all jokes apart, we say all these things while laughing and joking. But at that time, the actual intention was not to overcome it. It was to understand why this was happening and what I could learn from it. And trust me, I actually learnt a lot from it. And that is how I looked at it.”

Notably, Sonali shared that her approach to the disease involved changing how she viewed her body and the pain she was experiencing. She explained why the language of fighting or overcoming cancer felt negative to her.

As per the latest buzz, She shared, “Because I feel that when we say we have overcome something, it somehow feels like a fight. There is a sense of negativity somewhere. And, after all, it is our own body, isn’t it? The cancer cells are also our own cells. So, how can we fight ourselves? So how do I love my body the way it is? And I thought that maybe I should treat it with love. It’s very difficult to love something that was giving you so much pain. But I think that’s probably what worked for me. And that’s where it went.”

In further updates, Sonali was diagnosed with high-grade metastatic cancer in July 2018 and revealed the news publicly through a social media post. She subsequently travelled to New York for treatment and continued to share updates about her experience with followers. She also spoke about the physical and emotional challenges of the diagnosis in interviews. She achieved remission and was declared cancer-free in 2021.

On top of that, After overcoming cancer, Sonali made a comeback to acting. She has continued to explore different roles across films and television. She of late appeared in the web shows like Raakh and The Broken News. She also hosts reality game show Pati Patni Aur Panga with comedian Munawar Faruqui.

title: Delhi Police take down 300 social media posts in crackdown on ‘misinformation’ amid protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police is monitoring social media platforms to curb the spread of misinformation amid protests in the capital, with around 300 posts allegedly aimed at spreading rumours or creating public unrest taken down, police sources shared, according to PTI on Monday.

Adding to this, Delhi Police is monitoring various social media platforms to curb the spread of misinformation amid protests in the national capital (Sanjeev Verma/ Hindustan Times) The action comes amid heightened tensions following protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and allegations of police misconduct during the demonstrations. Police are scanning online platforms to identify fabricated videos, misleading claims and content that could potentially disturb public order.

Meanwhile, The police have also approached social media platform X, seeking the removal of objectionable and allegedly misleading content linked to the protests, according to PTI. Further action is being taken against posts found to be spreading misinformation or attempting to incite unrest, they added.

Notably, The crackdown on misleading content comes days after the arrest of a 24-year-old man, identified as Nadeem Ahmed, for allegedly using artificial intelligence (AI) tools to create and circulate a fabricated video depicting a police officer sexually harassing a woman journalist during a protest against the CEC.

As per the latest buzz, According to police, Ahmed allegedly circulated the video falsely portraying a police personnel in an objectionable manner. The case is being investigated separately from allegations of sexual harassment levelled against police personnel by women journalists.

In further updates, The development comes against the backdrop of protests organised by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar, where demonstrators demanded Kumar’s resignation over allegations of “vote chori”. Delhi Police had detained several protesters and key figures during the demonstrations, citing the lack of permission for the protest.

On top of that, The protests also triggered extensive security arrangements in central Delhi, with restrictions imposed around sensitive locations and metro services affected as authorities sought to prevent further disruption. Police personnel were deployed in large numbers to manage crowds and maintain order.

The demonstrations were also marked by allegations of violence and intimidation. Groups of men allegedly threatened and assaulted protesters and journalists in Connaught Place and near the MCD Civic Centre, even as security personnel were deployed across the city centre.
