title: Actor and MP Ravi Kishan on playing Lord Ram in Ayodhya Ki Ramleela: Dara hua hoon, can't afford to go wrong with Shri Ram
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star and Parliamentarian Ravi Kishan , who will be essaying the role of Shri Ram at Ayodhya Ki Ramleela on October 19 and 20 in New Delhi, with the event being telecast worldwide, says he is "scared" to play the deity on stage.

Adding to this, Star Ravi Kishan and his AI image in role of Shri Ram that he will perform at Ayodhya Ki Ram Leela in New Delhi on October 19 and 20 (Photo: Instagram and AI) He tells HT City, “Pehli baar Shri Ram ke roop dharan karne ka saubhagya mila and I pray and wish that He enters my body and gives me the energy to perform with grace. I have earlier played Parashuram and Kevat, as a kid I have played Mata Sita as well, and in a TV serial I have essayed the role of Shri Krishna as well, but this is different. I always want to play Shri Ram”

Meanwhile, Admitting that he is feeling more scared than he does on screen, he says, "Andar se dara hua hoon! I believe for an star that fear and scare is very important when you go on the stage, and this is the role of Shri Ram, so all the more reason to get it right… In the subconscious mind it's always there that any mistake does not happen."

Notably, Drawing a parallel between stage and screen, he says, "You can't afford to go wrong or improvise and have to stay within the bound script and character. I can have all the experience, but after all we are humans and anyone can commit mistakes! I try to give my 100% and that has resulted in the success of my roles in Mirzapur The Movie , Maamla Legal Hai and Laapatta Ladies ."

As per the latest buzz, He recalls that being a son of a priest, he has grown up listening to tales of Shri Ram and Mahadev, and now he is getting the chance. "It's not only about that act – chahrey pe soumyata, shaleenta, saiyam, ekagrita, because you portray the character of puroshon mein uttam Shri Ram. The entire world will watch and on live telecast over 50 crore rupees people will watch it on Doordarshan, OTT and YouTube live streamings."

In further updates, On his prep, he says, "The great thing is that we are in Navratri and I am fasting, so with a shudh body and pure soul I will essay the role. I am a vegetarian and have been on a special diet to look lean. Before the Ram Leela I will shave off my moustaches and am keeping myself calm and composed so that I can portray the role perfectly."
On top of that, Deep Saxena writes on Bollywood, OTT, television, food and culture for the daily Entertainment & Lifestyle supplement, HT City.

title: Ektaa Kapoor announces The Dirty Picture 2, 15 years after Vidya Balan’s National Award-winning performance: ‘There is a story to tell’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Vidya Balan won her first National Movie Award for her iconic performance in Ektaa Kapoor's The Dirty Picture . Fifteen years after the movie's theatrical rollout, Ektaa has now revealed its sequel. However, she has not revealed any details about the movie, including its central character, cast or rollout date.

Adding to this, Vidya Balan won the National Award for Best Star for her performance in The Dirty Picture. Ektaa Kapoor announces The Dirty Picture 2 In conversation with Ranveer Allahbadia on his podcast, Ektaa shared that she had been considering a sequel for some time but decided to move ahead only after finding a story she wanted to tell audiences.

Meanwhile, "One very big movie I'm making is The Dirty Picture 2. I'm planning it after 15 years. This time, I believe there is a story I want to tell. The Dirty Picture was about Silk Smitha. It was about a woman who was condemned for standing up against her sexuality. Ab sexuality is about your choice. I never saw her as a victim. I saw her as someone who celebrated her sexuality, and the movie did so well," she shared.
Notably, Ektaa added that, like the original, The Dirty Picture 2 would also revolve around one person's story. However, she did not reveal whose life would be at the centre of the sequel.

As per the latest buzz, Vidya won the National Movie Award for Best Star for her performance in The Dirty Picture. In 2012, the star spoke about her experience of making the movie and the memories she cherished from the project.

In further updates, She shared, “I just knew one thing we all were trying to make a good movie as long as you know that nothing is in your control. I was saying to Milan (Luthria- director) that the movie has rolled out two months back and now I want to watch the movie again. We have such wonderful memories with this movie I would be glad to watch this movie on DVD.”

On top of that, "I think the biggest award was The Dirty Picture. I got an opportunity to play Silk and to work with this team is the biggest award. Everybody have loved this movie and we are grateful for that," she added.

Directed by Milan Luthria and produced by Ektaa Kapoor and Shobha Kapoor, The Dirty Picture was rolled out in 2011. Inspired by the life of South Indian star Silk Smitha, the movie starred Vidya Balan in the lead role, alongside Naseeruddin Shah, Emraan Hashmi and Tusshar Kapoor. The movie explored the entertainment industry's treatment of women, sexuality and the price of fame.

title: Madhuri Dixit’s husband Dr Shriram Nene didn’t recognise Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan at their wedding reception, knew only Amitabh Bachchan
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Bollywood filmmaker and choreographer Farah Khan visited Madhuri Dixit and Dr Shriram Nene at their home for her latest cooking vlog, accompanied by her cook, Dilip. During the vlog, Farah discussed Madhuri and Dr Nene's love story. Dr Nene opened up that he felt like a prom king at their wedding reception because he did not know any of the celebrities who attended, apart from Amitabh Bachchan .

Adding to this, Dr Shriram Nene reveals he didn't know Shah Rukh Khan and Salman Khan at his and Madhuri Dixit's wedding reception. Dr Shriram Nene recalls his star-studded wedding reception Farah asked Dr Nene whether he really did not know who Madhuri was when he received the marriage proposal. Dr Nene verified that he did not. He opened up that he did not speak Hindi at the time and was living in Los Angeles. When Farah asked how he had not heard of Madhuri even while living in LA, he shared, "Because I grew up on Steven Spielberg, George Lucas, and Star Wars. I didn't watch Hindi films. Then we met and dated for three months. We just hit it off and got along, and after three months I proposed to her."

Meanwhile, Farah told Dr Nene that their relationship had been the biggest news in the Indian movie industry and had broken several hearts. Dr Nene opened up that they kept their relationship a secret before getting married at Madhuri's brother's house in the US.

Notably, Farah then recalled the grand reception Madhuri and Dr Nene hosted for the movie industry. Recalling the occasion, Dr Nene shared, "I didn't know anyone. It was like Prom King, you just waved at everyone and later look at the wedding album because you don't know anyone. The only person I knew was Amitabh Bachchan because I had seen Amar Akbar Anthony."

As per the latest buzz, When Farah asked Dr Nene whether he did not even know Shah Rukh Khan and Salman Khan, he verified that he did not. However, he added that all the celebrities had been very sweet to him at the reception.

In further updates, Madhuri married cardiovascular surgeon Dr Shriram Nene on October 17, 1999, when she was one of the biggest stars in Indian cinema. The couple tied the knot in a private, traditional ceremony at the residence of Madhuri's elder brother in Southern California, US. Their wedding came as a surprise to many followers, as the star was at the peak of her career, having delivered several hits, including Tezaab, Dil To Pagal Hai, Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!, and Khalnayak.

On top of that, Following their wedding, Madhuri moved to the United States and took a break from her acting career to focus on family life. The couple welcomed their first son, Arin, in 2003, followed by their second son, Ryan, in 2005. They returned to India in 2011, after which Madhuri gradually resumed working in films and television.

title: 'Shielding a predator': BJP stages protest over sexual harassment case against Congress MP at JNU
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday staged a protest and marched towards the Congress office, demanding action against Congress MP and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, who has been accused of sexual harassment.

Adding to this, The protest came after JNU terminated Akoijam’s services following an inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment involving female students. (Screengrab/BJPDelhi) BJP Mahila Morcha workers and other party members accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of shielding Akoijam and questioned whether “smash the patriarchy” was merely a political slogan.

Meanwhile, “Rahul Gandhi has been shielding the professor accused of sexual harassment. Congress talks about ‘Ladki hoon, lad sakti hoon’, but it has not taken any action against the professor,” Leela Singh, a member of the BJP’s SC Morcha, told HT.
Notably, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj also criticised Gandhi for his alleged “double standards” and accused him of shielding a “predator” in the Lok Sabha.

As per the latest buzz, “An internal committee report found that all the complaints of sexual harassment lodged by female students against the sitting Congress MP from Inner Manipur, Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, were true and recommended his dismissal,” Swaraj shared, according to news agency ANI.

In further updates, “I would like to ask if ‘smash the patriarchy’ is merely a political slogan. If not, why haven’t you taken action against your sitting MP yet? It is because of your double standards. He (Rahul Gandhi) not only gives a seat in the Lok Sabha to such an individual, a predator, but also shields him through his silence,” she added.
On top of that, Visuals showed protesters pushing against and climbing over barricades as they attempted to continue their march towards the Congress office.

Earlier on Monday, Delhi Police registered a first information report (FIR) against him at Vasant Kunj North police station following a complaint filed by the university’s chief security officer on October 11.

title: Nana Patekar’s autopsy CONFIRMS heart attack caused by blood clot in left main coronary artery: Report
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nana Patekar was 75. He was declared dead at 5.10 am after doctors attempted to revive him through cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for around 45 minutes. The star was at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, when he as per reports fell unwell.

Adding to this, According to a PTI report, the postmortem examination found that Nana suffered an acute heart attack after a blood clot blocked the left main coronary artery. The artery supplies blood to a significant portion of the heart.

Meanwhile, The autopsy report recorded the cause of death as, “acute myocardial infarction due to left main coronary artery thrombosis secondary to atherosclerotic occlusive coronary artery disease, a natural cause of death”.

Notably, The findings establish that Nana's death was due to natural causes. Doctors had initially suspected a heart attack when the star was brought to hospital, but the postmortem examination later provided the specific medical cause.

As per the latest buzz, Nana as per reports became unwell at his home in Dona Paula. His caretaker contacted a private hospital and requested an ambulance. Since the star's residence was located less than a kilometre from the hospital, an ambulance was dispatched to the house.
In further updates, Medical personnel as per reports began resuscitation efforts after reaching the residence. Doctors continued CPR for approximately 45 minutes but were unable to revive him.
On top of that, Nana was subsequently declared dead at 5.10 am on October 8. His mortal remains were later taken to Goa Medical College and Hospital for the postmortem examination.
Following the star's death, his son Malhar Patekar travelled to Goa to bring his father's mortal remains back to Maharashtra.

title: Aaditya, Amit Thackeray booked day after leading sit-in against Gyanesh Kumar
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Mumbai Police booked Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS)’s Amit Thackeray on Monday, a day after they led a sit-in demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s removal. The Shiv Sena (UBT) and MNS have revealed another round of agitation on Monday at 4pm.

Adding to this, MNS leader Amit Thackeray and Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Aditya Thackeray in Mumbai on Sunday. (PTI) On Sunday, police refused to allow any demonstration as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) called for a “farewell party” for Kumar. At least 300 people were detained before Amit Thackeray arrived, stopped a police van carrying protesters, and ensured that they got down before he got detained.

Meanwhile, His cousins, Aaditya and Tejas Thackeray, rushed to Shivaji Park, and led the sit-in outside Shiv Sena Bhavan. Around 1,000 MNS and Shiv Sena (UBT) workers joined them and caught police off guard.

Notably, A police officer shared the Thackerays and at least 25 others were booked under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, section 189 (unlawful assembly) and relevant sections of the Maharashtra Police Act.

As per the latest buzz, Aaditya Thackeray opened up that the agitation against Kumar would continue on Monday. He added the protesters were fighting against dictatorship and attempts to suppress dissent. “The action against protesters at August Kranti Maidan yesterday [Saturday] and Shivaji Park today [Sunday] was not expected of the Mumbai Police,” he shared.

In further updates, “They have begun acting like the Delhi Police, perhaps at the behest of political leaders in Delhi. Tushar Gandhi, the great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, was detained yesterday and rolled out hours later only after we protested.”

On top of that, He maintained that the protest was not political and was intended to support citizens raising concerns about the electoral system. “This is a protest by Bharat against the BJP [Bharatiya Janata Party], which is suppressing the voice of the people,” he shared. “It is a fight against traitor Gyanesh Kumar and will continue until he resigns.”

title: ‘Give way, listen to the thunderous sounds’: Tharoor quotes poem, backs Rahul over Gyanesh Kumar protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Monday backed his colleague Rahul Gandhi’s remarks that “this government will go”, in an apparent reference to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led Centre amid intensified protests against the Election Commission over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Adding to this, Congress MPs Shashi Tharoor and Rahul Gandhi. In a post on X, the Lok Sabha MP from Thiruvananthapuram put up a post of Gandhi that shared in Hindi: “Gyanesh Kumar will go. This government will go. Then the repair of democracy will begin”.
Meanwhile, Separately, Tharoor also posted verses from a poem of Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar', "Janatantra Ka Janma" (जनतंत्र का जन्म / “The Birth of Democracy”)”.

Notably, “But earthquakes happen and tornadoes do occur, When people raise their eyebrows in rage, Give way, listen to the thunderous sounds of the chariot of time, Abdicate the throne, for the people are coming to claim it,” the poem read.

As per the latest buzz, Gandhi has been leading the ongoing INDIA bloc’s protests against Kumar and “vote chori” in recent days. On Monday, he asked the CEC to turn approver and resign as the Opposition's fight was against the bigger powers that were behind him.

In further updates, "Resign, turn approver; you (Kumar) have made a mistake but you are not the mind behind the mistake," he shared at a press conference. "We know Gyanesh Kumar is unable to sleep at night; I am telling him directly 'you will not survive as CEC',” he added.

On top of that, The Opposition has been demanding the resignation of the CEC after a report by The Indian Express shared Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected on record at least 14 times over the last 10 months, mostly to decisions and orders related to the SIR of electoral rolls.

Under fire over objections raised by two of its commissioners, the poll panel asserted that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations in any institution and that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

title: Ranvir Shorey slams CJP's protest call, asks them to approach courts instead: ‘Hijacking the streets is the actual murder of democracy’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Ranvir Shorey has weighed in on the row surrounding the detention of Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders ahead of their planned protest in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He argued that protesters should turn to the courts and democratic institutions rather than take to the streets. His remarks come amid criticism from several Bollywood actors, including Huma Qureshi , Sonakshi Sinha and Vijay Varma , over the authorities' handling of the demonstration.

Adding to this, Ranvir Shorey says protests should be the last resort in a democracy. Ranvir Shorey slams CJP for protesting On Sunday, Ranvir took to X and shared a video of CJP spokesperson Sourav Das appealing to citizens to take to the streets and not retreat. Reacting to the video, he wrote, "Show your numbers in Parliament and the ballot, not the streets! And if the way to those seems unjust, show the courts! That is the democratic way! Hijacking the streets and holding the public infrastructure and law and order machinery to ransom is the actual “murder of democracy”!"

Meanwhile, He added, "Protests in a democracy are meant to be a last resort. Not a way to circumvent the judiciary’s or legislative domain! Your “right to dissent” cannot turn into 7-days-a-week “protests” that hijack the country and make life hell for the rest of us! Only anarchists, attention seekers or morons would protest without exercising the legal remedies already available."

Notably, When an X user responded by saying that Ranvir did not know that the 'CJI has been compromised as well', the star appeared to mock the claim, writing, "Ever-growing list: I am compromised, Other voters are compromised, Media is compromised, Parliament is compromised, PMO is compromised, CEC is compromised, SC is compromised…Only daphli banging, dubiously funded mobs of parties that didn’t win elections on the streets are believable."

As per the latest buzz, The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, planned a protest in Delhi on October 10, 2026, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The demonstration was scheduled to take place at Jantar Mantar. However, ahead of the protest, Delhi Police detained Dipke and two other CJP leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, at Delhi airport shortly after they arrived from Mumbai. The three were later rolled out. Protests continued in Delhi on Sunday.

In further updates, On Monday, Ashutosh Ranka gave Delhi Police 24 hours to announce a date for a protest at Jantar Mantar, warning that the CJP would decide its next course of action if it did not receive a response within the deadline.

On top of that, Meanwhile, security has been tightened in central Delhi ahead of a protest march to the Supreme Court led by the INDIA bloc. Barricades have been erected at several locations, and entry and exit at certain metro stations will remain closed from 6 am to 4 pm on October 12, 2026, for security reasons.

title: 'Poora desh Jantar Mantar banega': Abhijeet Dipke as site loses ‘designated protest venue’ tag
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday reacted to the Delhi Police's decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a designated protest venue, saying the entire country would now become a site for demonstrations.

Adding to this, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke speaks to the media at Dr BR Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur, after being rolled out from the custody of Delhi Police. (ANI) “They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it’s no longer a protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!” Dipke wrote on X.

Meanwhile, The reaction came after a Delhi Police circular on Monday opened up that Jantar Mantar would no longer be a designated venue for protests and demonstrations. The circular also named three alternative locations for holding demonstrations in the national capital.

Notably, According to the Delhi Police circular, the Ministry of Home Affairs had constituted a committee to examine alternative venues for citizens to exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations.

As per the latest buzz, Based on the committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a designated protest site. The three new venues identified for demonstrations are Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in Shahdara.
In further updates, The circular shared detailed and revised standard operating procedures for organising protests at the three venues would be issued separately.

On top of that, Jantar Mantar has been a focal point of youth-led protests since June, led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founded by Dipke. The demonstrations had previously drawn attention over alleged examination irregularities and demands for accountability from the government.

The site came into focus again last month after an investigative report raised questions about Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities. The report gave fresh momentum to Opposition allegations of “vote chori” (vote theft) linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

In further updates, He also credited Kashyap for his support. Anurag and Ranjan sir from the very beginning...They never asked us to simplify it or make it easier. That belief gave us the freedom to make the movie exactly as we felt it, and I'm grateful to have walked this path with them," he added.
On top of that, Kashyap shared the movie offers Pingal's fresh approach, which "challenges the filmmaking norms".

"I met Rohan at a post lab, where he showed me some of the visuals he had been creating for his movie's pitch, and I was surprised that they created them all by themselves far away from where all the VFX studios were," he shared.

title: Gulshan Devaiah recalls weeping after Irrfan’s death, says he ‘didn’t know’ he liked the actor so much
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

From playing a menacing villain in Guns & Gulaabs to a caring partner in Badhaai Do, Gulshan Devaiah has shown his versatility as an star. Yet, across the many characters he has played, there is a certain stillness in his performances that brings to mind the late Irrfan . In an exclusive interaction with Hindustan Times, Gulshan opened up about how the legendary star influenced his craft, admitting that while he has consciously and subconsciously picked up aspects of Irrfan’s acting, he has never tried to imitate him.

Adding to this, Gulshan Devaiah spoke about Irrfan’s influence on his acting. 'Irrfan has been a huge influence on me' When asked whether Irrfan had influenced his acting, Gulshan shared, “Absolutely, both consciously and subconsciously. I never try to copy him, but Irrfan was a huge influence on me throughout my career. Since I didn't go to drama school, I learned acting by observing great performers. However, I was very conscious that I didn't want to copy anyone — whether Irrfan, Manoj Bajpayee, Daniel Day-Lewis, Robert De Niro, or Kate Winslet. And that's how I learned.”

Meanwhile, Gulshan also spoke about the uniqueness of Irrfan’s performances and how, despite not fitting the conventional mould of a leading man, the star had an undeniable ability to draw audiences towards him.

Notably, He shared, “Irrfan had this quality that you didn't know what he would do next, and many times he didn't do much; he would hold back. Genetically, he had those big, god-gifted eyes that held your attention even when he was doing very little on screen. He used them really well. Sometimes he would deliver lines without even looking at his co-star. He was doing things that were really different. He would deliver dialogues differently, yet there was this magnetic attraction to him, and one wouldn’t say that he was not as good-looking as Hrithik Roshan or Shah Rukh Khan or Salman Khan, but somehow he would draw attention. So certainly, he was one of the greatest influences among many actors.”

As per the latest buzz, While Gulshan closely observed Irrfan’s performances to hone his own acting skills, he had not realised just how deeply connected he felt to the star until he heard of his death. Recalling his reaction to the news, Gulshan shared, “I remember weeping on the phone with my mother when the news broke. He was truly a one-of-a-kind star. This is why his death, not only for me, but for millions of people, felt very personal, like a family member has passed away. I was talking to my mother and weeping, and my mother was like ‘I didn’t know you liked him so much’, and I was like, ‘Yeah, neither did I.’”

In further updates, Gulshan is currently gearing up for the rollout of his next movie, Little Thomas, which follows a curious young boy who desperately wants a sibling. Directed by Kaushal Oza, the movie is set to rollout on October 23.

title: 'Cops slapped us, hit our private parts, took us 30-40 km away': Protesters detained in Delhi anti-EC stir
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The second day of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest witnessed detentions of more than 700 persons, some of whom were detained for almost seven hours, with their phones snatched and taken to detention centres, which are 30-40 km away.

Adding to this, Security personnel detain a demonstrator during a protest demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities linked to the "special intensive revision" (SIR), near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on October 11. (AFP) On Sunday evening, many lawyers and activists posted SOS messages on X and other social media platforms to seek help for the detainees.
Meanwhile, HT spoke to two of the detainees who shared how they were detained, targeted, assaulted and whisked off in prison vans to Pandwalan Khurd.

Notably, One of the detainees, Arjun Unnikrishnan (30), is a researcher and a lawyer who was at Connaught Place around 3-3.30 pm on Sunday to protest against the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, when he was detained. He shared he spent almost seven hours in detention in different parts, which was a complete nightmare for him.

As per the latest buzz, “I had just reached Connaught Place when my friends and I saw a group of police personnel detaining a couple. The police personnel then approached us and started pushing us. They shoved us inside a DTC bus along with locals who were not even part of the protest. We were taken close to Palika Bazaar side. Soon, the police started acting like mad people. They first made us sit on the road in rows. They snatched our phones...many of us had tried to record them. People who refused to share their phone passwords were humiliated and abused. Nobody had a choice,” Arjun told HT.

In further updates, “In front of me, a young boy was mentally tortured as they slapped him four times and then took his phone to open his phone's gallery. Almost 10 cops were looking at a young boy's phone and laughing. We were all very scared. Then, a senior officer came who pretended to be a good police officer as he scolded other officials and assured us we would be safe and rolled out if we cooperated. By then, we had been slapped and abused and were scared, so we agreed to cooperate,” he added.

On top of that, "But then, they brought in a jail van. We entered the jail van in a line. The moment we entered, we saw 3-4 police personnel. One by one, they slapped us, hit our private parts, and kicked us on the chest and back. Nobody could even run because it's a small, cage-like van. This was all in the middle of CP. There were four minors. I know this because when the police were taking our details, they revealed their names and ages. We raised our voice, but the police were not ready to listen," Arjun further shared .

He alleged that the detention bus took them from CP to Chhawla, where it halted for 10-20 minutes before leaving. By then, one of the protesters, who had managed to hide his phone, had contacted a lawyer and sent his live location.

title: Vidyut Jammwal says he bagged Street Fighter without an agent, lauds Priyanka Chopra’s global impact and 'what she has done for the country’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Vidyut Jammwal will make his Hollywood debut in Kitao Sakurai’s Street Fighter as Dhalsim, the iconic character from the popular video game franchise. Ahead of the movie’s rollout, the star opened up about how he bagged the role in the live-action adaptation, revealing that he neither hired an agent in Hollywood nor actively looked for opportunities there. Instead, it was the director’s research into the character that led him to Vidyut .

Adding to this, Vidyut Jammwal in a still from Street Fighter. Vidyut Jammwal landed Street Fighter role without an agent in Hollywood In conversation with News18, Vidyut shared that the movie’s Japanese-American director, Kitao Sakurai, knows India well. He explained how the filmmaker’s research for the characters eventually led him to the star, and how the role came his way after an audition and several conversations.

Meanwhile, “Kitao’s very passionate and he was very sure about the eleven main fighters in the movie. His research is what led him to me, and that’s what destiny has done. I got a call from these guys and I got to speak to the director. We had a lot of chats, but before he had a conversation with me, he had watched most of my interviews and a lot of my movies. To have a conversation with someone who’s so well-prepared about what he’s looking for, made me feel I’m in safe hand,” he shared.

Notably, Vidyut also spoke about opportunities for Indian actors in Hollywood, especially as several Indian stars, including Alia Bhatt, Deepika Padukone, Dhanush and Randeep Hooda, have appeared in international productions. He gave a special mention to Priyanka Chopra and the impact her work in Hollywood has had on Indian cinema.

As per the latest buzz, When asked whether more Indian actors starring in Hollywood films could lead to more opportunities for others from the country, Vidyut shared, “I can’t vouch for that but it could be possible. India’s already on the global map. People know india so well. All these actors I worked with on Street Fighter have been to India several times. The director is Japanese-American and he knows about our country more than many Indians do. He’s one of the few people I’ve met, who can pronounce the martial art (kalaripayattu) that I do with brilliance. These guys already know about it. But I can mention Priyanka Chopra for sure. What she has done for the country is incredible in terms of cinema."

In further updates, Street Fighter is an soon-to-release live-action action movie directed by Kitao Sakurai and based on Capcom’s popular video game franchise of the same name. Vidyut plays Dhalsim, the Indian yoga master and warrior known to followers of the video games for his distinctive fighting style.

title: 'Tell us in 24 hours or we will': CJP's ultimatum over Jantar Mantar protest amid access restrictions
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) co-convener Ashutosh Ranka on Monday gave the Delhi Police 24 hours to provide a date for holding a protest at Jantar Mantar, warning that the party would announce its next course of action if no response came within the deadline. Ranka and fellow co-convener Saurav Dass entered the Parliament Street police station to press for a date.

Adding to this, A protester is detained by police during a protest demanding the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar. (AP Photo) “Jantar Mantar is the designated protest site and we are here to seek dates on which we can carry out our protest,” Ranka shared.
Meanwhile, “Where should I carry out our protest? They should tell us in the next 24 hours how we can proceed with the protest. Otherwise, we will give our next call,” he added.

Notably, The development comes amid heightened tensions in Delhi over protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

As per the latest buzz, The Delhi Police denied permission for CJP’s proposed October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar, citing the short notice given by the organisers, alleged violations during previous demonstrations and concerns over public safety, traffic and law and order.

In further updates, The police shared the intimation was received on October 7, only three days before the proposed demonstration, while the prescribed guidelines require applications to be submitted at least 10 days in advance.
On top of that, The proposed protest was intended to press for Kumar’s resignation. CJP had revealed the demonstration as part of its campaign against alleged irregularities in the SIR process.
The police also cited the group’s previous protests at Jantar Mantar, alleging that an earlier demonstration continued beyond the permitted period and led to law-and-order problems.

title: In special sitting, Bombay high court in Goa orders release of anti-EC protesters
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Bombay High Court in Goa held a special sitting on Sunday evening and ordered the immediate rollout of protesters detained during demonstrations seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Adding to this, Hundreds of people, including environmentalists Claude and Norma Alvares and political leaders, participated in the protest. (HT sourced) The protesters were detained at Panjim's Azad Maidan after they breached a security cordon that was formed on the ground's precinct, ran towards the ground’s centre and waved the national flag.
Meanwhile, Seven protesters were detained by the police and bundled into a state transport corporation bus, before being taken to Pernem Police Station more than 30-km north of Panaji.

Notably, “Considering that there are no prohibitory orders under section 163 of the BNSS, we are of the opinion that the detention may not have been authorised… for the moment without entering into the row and the correctness of the detention order, considering that senior advocate appearing on behalf of the detainees gives an undertaking that the detainees would not protest at Azad Maidan, Panaji, tonight, we direct the PI Panaji Police Station to rollout the seven seven persons forthwith,” the bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar shared.
As per the latest buzz, The detainees were represented by senior advocate Norma Alvares.
In further updates, The protesters affiliated to the Cockroach Janta Party had planned a sit-in protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

On top of that, Among those detained was local CCP (Corporation of the City) corporator Jack Sukhija and Goa CJP unit lead protester Amreen Shaikh among others. Former Allahabad High Court chief justice Ferdino Rebello was among those who had gathered at the site in support of the movement.

title: 'Don't drag Supreme Court into politics': CJI Surya Kant amid Delhi protests row
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday shared the Supreme Court should not be “dragged into any politics” amid the ongoing protests against the alleged crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi, urging lawyers to ensure that the functioning of the top court and the movement of lawyers, court staff and litigants remains unhindered.

Adding to this, ‘SC can’t be allowed to become disruption site’: CJI after plea on Delhi police action (PTI) “There should not be any obstruction in the functioning of the court. There should not be any impediment in the movement of the lawyers, their clerks, court staff or litigants,” the CJI told Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai, who mentioned a fresh petition concerning the detention of lawyers and the suspension of internet services.
Meanwhile, Making it clear that the court had no objection to democratic activities, CJI Kant shared lawyers were free to protest but should do so at designated places.

Notably, “Every member of the Bar can also protest. Wherever there is a designated place to protest, you can protest,” he told senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, who also mentioned a separate petition for listing. CJI Kant added that he had already appealed to the protesters.

As per the latest buzz, The observations came a day after a special bench of justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued a series of directions to protect the right to peaceful protest, restore freedom of movement and ensure that no person was detained except in accordance with the procedure established by law. The bench also directed that metro and railway services operate normally, internet connectivity remain undisturbed and restrictions around court complexes be removed to ensure access to justice.

In further updates, Rai sought the listing of the SCBA’s fresh petition on Tuesday, when the court is scheduled to hear the other batch of matters arising from the protests. The CJI agreed to list the plea but asked the Bar to ensure that the court’s functioning was not affected.

On top of that, “Alright, we will list it. But you must also see that democratic activities take place smoothly. There is no difficulty with that. But just see to it that at least the Supreme Court functioning is not affected,” shared the CJI.
When Rai pointed out that the lawyers were protesting peacefully, the CJI reiterated his concern about the institution being drawn into the political contest surrounding the demonstrations.

title: Drishyam 3 worldwide box office collection day 10: Ajay Devgn film beats Border 2's lifetime haul in just 10 days
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window performance day 10: Ajay Devgn ’s Drishyam The Conclusion has emerged as one of the biggest box-office successes of 2026 so far. The crime thriller, billed as the final instalment in the Drishyam franchise, has crossed the ₹ 450 crore rupees mark worldwide within 10 days of its rollout. Despite a slowdown during the week, the movie has maintained a strong run and is closing in on the ₹ 500 crore rupees milestone. It has also secured the position of the second-highest-grossing movie of the year so far.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window earnings day 10: Ajay Devgn leads the thriller. Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window performance According to Sacnilk, Drishyam 3 collected ₹ 176.50 crore rupees net in India over its opening weekend, securing one of the biggest starts for a Hindi movie. It recorded the seventh-highest opening weekend for a Hindi rollout, coming close to the figures posted by Sultan while surpassing the opening-weekend collections of War and Tiger 3. The movie continued to draw audiences through the weekdays, with its collections witnessing only moderate declines. After wrapping up its first week with ₹ 245 crore rupees net in India, the Abhishek Pathak directorial began its second week on a strong note, earning ₹ 14.50 crore rupees on Friday.

Meanwhile, The thriller then added ₹ 49 crore rupees over its second weekend, taking its domestic net collection to ₹ 309 crore rupees. Its overseas performance has been relatively more restrained, although the movie has continued to register steady business in international markets. Trade sources indicate that it collected ₹ 6 crore rupees on its 10th day, pushing its overseas gross earnings to ₹ 109 crore rupees. With these figures, Drishyam The Conclusion has taken its worldwide gross collection to ₹ 479 crore rupees, bringing it within touching distance of the ₹ 500 crore rupees mark.

Notably, Ajay Devgn's Drishyam The Conclusion has not only become the highest-grosser of his career, but has also positioned itself as the second highest-grossing movie of 2026 so far. The movie surpassed the lifetime hauls of Sunny Deol, Varun Dhawan and Diljit Dosanjh's Border 2 ( ₹ 450 crore rupees worldwide) and Hanuman Ansh ( ₹ 435 crore rupees worldwide). It is now only behind Ranveer Singh and Aditya Dhar's Dhurandhar The Revenge ( ₹ 1813 crore rupees worldwide).

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Abhishek Pathak, Drishyam 3 brings back Ajay Devgn’s Vijay Salgaonkar, along with Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav, and Kamlesh Sawant. Saurabh Shukla also reprises his role from the second part in a cameo.

In further updates, The story picks up six months after the events of Drishyam 2, with Vijay Salgaonkar (Ajay Devgn) and his family—wife Nandini (Shriya Saran), and daughters Anju and Anu—living under the shadow of the past murder case, waiting for the legal file to permanently close. Officer Rajveer reopens the cold case with fresh intent, targeting the local police station where Sam's body was hidden beneath the foundation years ago, hunting for fresh DNA or physical proof. The movie culminates in a high-stakes ego clash and courtroom/investigative showdown between Vijay and Rajveer, bringing a definitive stop to the franchise.

title: International organisations condemn detention of journalists during Delhi protests, urge police to uphold press freedom
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) on Sunday urged Delhi Police to refrain from targeting journalists covering protests in the capital and honour the government’s assurance to the Supreme Court that media personnel would not be impeded in performing their duties.

Adding to this, Security personnel detain demonstrators during a protest near Jantar Mantar on Sunday. (Vipin Kumar/HT) CPJ is a US-based independent organisation that documents attacks on journalists and advocates for press freedom worldwide. Other international organisations, such as Reporters Without Borders (RSF) and the United Nations Human Rights Office (OHCHR), also expressed concern.

Meanwhile, “At least six journalists, including those from mainstream news organisations such as The Indian Express and Hindustan Times, were temporarily detained by Delhi Police,” CPJ shared in a post on X.

Notably, “CPJ calls on Delhi Police to honour the government’s assurance to the Supreme Court that journalists will not be impeded in their professional duties and to refrain from targeting journalists covering the protests,” it added.

As per the latest buzz, They shared India, as the world’s largest democracy, had a special responsibility to uphold press freedom and protect journalists’ constitutional right to report without interference.

In further updates, These detentions took place during the October 10 protests, planned by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

On top of that, Authorities imposed curbs without precedent in Delhi, ordering the gates of 45 metro stations to be shut, cutting mobile internet across central Delhi, cancelling trains into the city, deploying more than 40,000 Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) personnel, and installing barricades and spike strips ahead of the protest.

There were reports of journalists being detained around Jantar Mantar. Posts and videos on social media showed the detained journalists flashing their press cards from the buses transporting detainees.
